epic.title: [EPIC] Phase 0 — Preserve the baseline and establish the repository
epic.body:
Phase 0 is the hardware-first foundation of the punchCraft · Puncheokie project. It must complete before any BLE code is written against the physical FightCamp v1 trackers, because the official app can still connect today and that reference behavior will disappear the moment the tracker is repaired, replaced, or its firmware drifts. See spec §22 Phase 0, §12.1, §12.2, §11.2, §23 Story 1, and §29 references R1–R4.

## Objectives

- Preserve official-app behavior while it is still possible.
- Record development-device versions (tablet model, Android version, official-app version, tracker firmware where visible).
- Establish a reproducible Expo Android build that installs on the tablet over USB.

## Milestones

- M01 — Baseline preserved & official-app captures archived
- M02 — Installable Expo development build

## Definition of done

- The project builds on Windows, installs on the tablet, and the official-app reference captures are preserved outside the phone.
- Both trackers are inventoried and their left/right identity is confirmed per R1/R2.
- A known-good APK artifact and lockfile exist and are archived alongside the reference captures.

## Non-goals

- No BLE code beyond the bounded scan / connect / notify compatibility spike required by §11.2 and §23 Story 1 (M02-01) — full BLE subsystem work begins in Phase 1.
- No writes to any GATT characteristic other than the standard CCCD descriptor required to enable a notify subscription (§12.1).
- No protocol decoding or FightCampV1Adapter work — that is Phase 2.
- No punchCraft session UI, no Puncheokie program engine, no Spotify integration.
- No writes to any unknown GATT characteristic — writes stay behind observed-command allowlists and developer mode (§7.2C, §12.1).

## Sub-issues

GitHub auto-populates the sub-issue list for this epic from the linked issues; do not maintain it by hand.

issues.title: Record tablet model, Android version, and tracker hardware inventory
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 0 / M01 requires the exact development-device baseline captured before any code is written, per spec §22 Phase 0 tasks 1–2 and §12.1 ("preserve the official-app baseline while it can still connect"). This issue records tablet identity and both trackers as durable evidence that later capability reports can be tied back to.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Tablet manufacturer, model, marketing name, Android release + API level, and build fingerprint recorded in `docs/hardware-baseline.md`.
- [ ] Both trackers fully charged before inventory (photo of the official app's battery indicator if visible).
- [ ] Each tracker photographed showing case color, any serial or FCC ID markings, and physical labels applied for red/right and blue/left per R1/R2.
- [ ] Official-app version and build number recorded from Android settings.
- [ ] Files committed under `docs/hardware-baseline.md` with photos referenced from `docs/hardware-baseline/`.
- [ ] Explicitly covers §22 Phase 0 task 2: both trackers are fully charged AND photographed AND physically labeled before any HCI capture (M01-04) begins — this is the pre-requisite for §12.2 step 1.

## Non-goals

- No BLE scans, no connection attempts, no HCI capture (covered by M01-03/M01-04).
- No firmware update attempts — the goal is to freeze what exists today.

## Notes

- References: §22 Phase 0 tasks 1–2, §12.1, R1 (FightCamp connection guide), R2 (Hykso left/right color).
- Hardware required: tablet + both trackers + official app still installed.
- Output feeds M02-06 (build-info screen surfaces app/OS/dependency versions; hardware baseline stays as an ops doc).

issues.title: Confirm red/right and blue/left assignment and verify trackers in official app
issues.body:
## Context

Before we can label any capture with hand identity we must confirm which tracker the vendor's app treats as left and which as right, per §22 Phase 0 tasks 3–4 and R1/R2. This is the last chance to verify the trackers still function with the official app.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Official app onboarding walked through end-to-end with both trackers.
- [ ] Red tracker confirmed as right hand and blue as left hand per R1/R2, or the deviation recorded.
- [ ] Screen recording of the official app showing both trackers connected simultaneously, saved to `docs/hardware-baseline/official-app-both-connected.mp4`.
- [ ] If either tracker fails to pair, the failure mode and any error text is captured to `docs/hardware-baseline.md` and the risk register in spec §24 is updated.
- [ ] Physical labels from M01-01 verified against the official app's assignment.

## Non-goals

- No BLE inspection outside the official app.
- No firmware update.

## Notes

- References: §22 Phase 0 tasks 3–4, §12.1, R1, R2, R3 (Hykso getting started).
- Hardware required: tablet + both trackers + official app.
- Blocks M01-04 (need to know left/right for labeled scenarios).

issues.title: Enable Android Bluetooth HCI snoop logging on the tablet
issues.body:
## Context

M01 / Phase 0 task 5 requires capturing controlled official-app sessions with HCI snoop logging (§22 Phase 0, §12.2). Snoop logging is a developer-options toggle on Android and must be enabled and validated before any labeled scenario is captured.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Developer options enabled on the tablet; the enable procedure recorded in `docs/dev-setup.md` including exact settings-path.
- [ ] Bluetooth HCI snoop log toggle enabled and Bluetooth restarted so the toggle takes effect.
- [ ] A short throwaway capture is exported via `adb bugreport` and the `btsnoop_hci.log` located and verified non-empty.
- [ ] The extracted `btsnoop_hci.log` opens in Wireshark on Windows and shows ATT/GATT frames from the official app pairing sequence.
- [ ] `docs/dev-setup.md` records the exact adb command used to extract the log and the Wireshark version verified.

## Non-goals

- No captures of the controlled §12.2 scenarios yet — that is M01-04.
- No protocol interpretation of the frames.

## Notes

- References: §12.2 steps 3, 6–7; §22 Phase 0 task 5.
- Hardware required: tablet + USB cable + Windows workstation with Wireshark installed.
- Files affected: `docs/dev-setup.md`.

issues.title: Capture controlled official-app scenarios with HCI snoop logging
issues.body:
## Context

This is the single most time-sensitive item in Phase 0. Per §12.1 the official-app baseline must be preserved while it can still connect, and §12.2 defines the exact controlled scenarios that must be captured at least three times each so that later decoder work in Phase 2 has evidence to work from. M01 / Phase 0 task 5.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Each of the following controlled scenarios from §12.2 is executed at least three times with the official app: connect only (no punches); start and stop an empty session; one left punch; one right punch; exactly five left punches with two-second gaps; exactly five alternating punches; slow / normal / fast punches of the same type; disconnect, throw known punches, reconnect; sleep and wake; tracker A only vs tracker B only.
- [ ] For every run: trackers fully charged, left/right identity confirmed, screen recording of the official app with a visible wall clock, and a fresh Bluetooth HCI snoop log covering the run.
- [ ] Each run is logged in `docs/captures/official-app/index.md` with scenario name, run number, tablet wall time, tracker battery, and pointer to the paired snoop log + screen recording.
- [ ] Snoop logs are exported from the tablet to the Windows workstation and never mutated in place.
- [ ] The capture set is stored under `docs/captures/official-app/<scenario>/<runN>/` with immutable raw files (§12.1 "keep raw captures immutable").

## Non-goals

- No Wireshark filtering or protocol notes — that is M01-06.
- No writes to the trackers outside the official app.
- Do not attempt firmware upgrades between scenarios.

## Notes

- References: §12.1, §12.2 controlled scenarios, §22 Phase 0 task 5.
- Hardware required: tablet + both trackers + official app + Windows workstation for export.
- This story is the input for M01-05, M01-06, and eventually Phase 2 decoder tests (§21.2, §12.7).

issues.title: Export HCI snoop logs and reference captures to Windows and archive off-device
issues.body:
## Context

§12.1 requires raw captures to be kept immutable and Phase 0 DoD requires the reference captures to live outside the phone. This task moves the M01-04 output off the tablet into a durable archive.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All snoop logs, screen recordings, and per-run metadata from M01-04 are copied to the Windows workstation under `docs/captures/official-app/` and hashed (SHA-256) into a manifest.
- [ ] The manifest `docs/captures/official-app/MANIFEST.sha256` lists every file with its hash and byte size.
- [ ] A second copy exists on an external drive or cloud location documented in `docs/captures/official-app/README.md` (path only, not credentials).
- [ ] Files in the archive are marked read-only.
- [ ] Tablet copies retained until Phase 1 Story 4 lands, then may be deleted only after re-hashing confirms the archive still matches the manifest.

## Non-goals

- No transcoding or trimming of raw files.
- No interpretation of frames.

## Notes

- References: §12.1, §22 Phase 0 DoD ("reference captures preserved outside the phone").
- Hardware required: tablet + Windows workstation.
- Depends on M01-04.

issues.title: Isolate ATT/GATT traffic in Wireshark and produce baseline observation notes
issues.body:
## Context

§12.2 steps 7–8 require ATT/GATT traffic to be isolated and correlated with the physical action for each captured run. This task produces the first observation notes — evidence-only, no decoder work — that will seed the Phase 2 FightCampV1Adapter (§12.3) and inform the Phase 1 GATT inventory.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A Wireshark filter recipe for ATT/GATT and for the trackers' BD_ADDR is documented in `docs/protocol/wireshark-recipe.md`.
- [ ] For each scenario captured in M01-04 a short notes file `docs/protocol/observations/<scenario>.md` lists: services discovered by the official app, characteristics written to, characteristics subscribed for notifications, and any pattern that repeats across runs.
- [ ] Every observation is tagged with a confidence level (low / medium / high) and cites the specific run(s) it came from (§12.1: "record all hypotheses with confidence and evidence").
- [ ] Notes explicitly avoid claiming any physical unit for a numeric field (§4.3 — no impact speed / force / power / energy / punch strength language; use "tracker-reported velocity" only when the field is confirmed).
- [ ] No proposed writes to unknown characteristics are recorded — observation only (§12.1).

## Non-goals

- No code — this is analysis of archived captures.
- No FightCampV1Adapter, no fixtures — those are Phase 2.

## Notes

- References: §12.1, §12.2, §12.3, §4.3.
- Hardware required flag stays true because captures were tracker-derived, though execution is on archived files from M01-05.
- Output feeds Phase 1 Story 4 (GATT inventory) and Phase 2 decoder work.

issues.title: Preserve the official-app APK and reference bundle outside the tablet
issues.body:
## Context

The official FightCamp v1 companion app is already unsupported (see §1). Phase 0 DoD requires reference captures to live outside the phone, and to keep the ability to reproduce the baseline we must also preserve the app binary itself before an OS update or vendor takedown removes it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Installed official-app APK extracted from the tablet via `adb shell pm path` + `adb pull` and stored under `docs/hardware-baseline/official-app/`.
- [ ] APK SHA-256 added to `docs/hardware-baseline/official-app/MANIFEST.sha256` together with version code, version name, and target SDK from `aapt` / `apkanalyzer`.
- [ ] APK archived to the same external location as the captures from M01-05 and file marked read-only.
- [ ] `docs/hardware-baseline/official-app/README.md` records provenance (device pulled from, date, tablet build fingerprint) and states that the archive is for internal reference / interoperability analysis only.

## Non-goals

- No decompilation or static analysis in this issue.
- No redistribution of the APK.

## Notes

- References: §12.1, §22 Phase 0 DoD, §1.
- Hardware required: tablet + Windows workstation.
- Depends on M01-01.

issues.title: BLE library × Expo SDK compatibility spike on tablet
issues.body:
## Context

Sprint 1 Story 1 (§23) and §11.2 require that we lock exact Expo, React Native, and BLE-library versions after a minimal scan/connect spike passes on the target tablet. Expo SDK 57.0.15 is current (RN 0.86 / React 19.2), Expo documents that SDK 54 is the last version where the New Architecture can be disabled, and upstream react-native-ble-plx 3.5.1 (released 2026-02-17) still has open issue #1277 with connect crashes reported and no New-Architecture entry. This spike picks a stack we can build the rest of Phase 1 on. This is a go/no-go gate — §24 risk register treats 'Expo/BLE dependency incompatibility' as requiring a minimal spike and exact version lock before any further BLE work.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Each candidate stack, in order, is attempted on the tablet inside a throwaway `spikes/ble-stack-<n>/` project until the first one passes: 1) Expo SDK 57 + `@sfourdrinier/react-native-ble-plx` 3.9.3; 2) Expo SDK 57 + `react-native-ble-manager` 12.5.1; 3) Expo SDK 54 + `react-native-ble-plx` 3.5.1 with `"newArchEnabled": false`; 4) Expo SDK 57 + upstream `react-native-ble-plx` 3.5.1 (only if 1–3 fail).
- [ ] A stack "passes" only when on the physical tablet the throwaway app can: request Android 12+ BLUETOOTH_SCAN / BLUETOOTH_CONNECT, run a bounded scan, connect to one FightCamp v1 tracker, discover services, and subscribe to at least one notify characteristic and receive at least one callback (no writes to unknown characteristics — §12.1).
- [ ] Result recorded in `docs/decisions/0001-ble-stack.md` with: which stack was locked, exact versions (Expo SDK, RN, React, BLE library, `expo-build-properties`, Android compileSdk / targetSdk / minSdk / NDK), evidence log for each attempted stack (build error, runtime crash, or pass), and links to the spike branch.
- [ ] Decision references R6 (react-native-ble-plx), R7 (Android BLE permissions), R8 (Android BLE overview), §11.2, §11.3.
- [ ] Spike artifacts kept in `spikes/` and NOT merged into the main app scaffold — the decision doc is the deliverable.
- [ ] The decision doc records these facts verbatim: Expo SDK 57.0.15 latest (RN 0.86 / React 19.2); Expo docs quote "SDK 54 is the last SDK version where the New Architecture can be disabled"; upstream react-native-ble-plx 3.5.1 released 2026-02-17 with no New-Architecture entry; issue #1277 open with connect crashes reported.
- [ ] Go/no-go: if none of the four stacks pass, Phase 1 is HALTED and the risk is escalated per §24 before any further BLE work is planned.

## Non-goals

- No punchCraft or Puncheokie UI.
- No writes to unknown GATT characteristics beyond a single safe notify subscription.
- No FightCampV1Adapter — that is Phase 2.

## Notes

- References: §23 Story 1, §11.2, §11.3, §12.1, §24, R6, R7, R8, R9.
- Hardware required: tablet + at least one tracker.
- Blocks M02-02, M02-03, M02-04, M02-05.

issues.title: Scaffold TypeScript-strict Expo project with expo-router tabs and §16 folder layout
issues.body:
## Context

Sprint 1 Story 1 (§23) and §22 Phase 0 task 6 require a TypeScript-strict Expo project. §16 fixes the on-disk layout so BLE, protocol, capture, domain, storage, state, components, and diagnostics have defined homes and §15.1 forbids domain code from importing RN / Expo / SQLite / BLE. This scaffold is the shape the rest of the app grows into.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Expo project created with the SDK version locked by M02-01, TypeScript, and `tsconfig.json` `"strict": true` (no `any`, no `noImplicitAny` disabled).
- [ ] `expo-router` installed with a two-tab skeleton for punchCraft and Puncheokie plus a Velocity Lab entry (per §6 / R5), each route a placeholder screen.
- [ ] Folder tree in `src/` matches §16 verbatim (empty `.gitkeep` placeholders allowed for folders that will be populated in later phases).
- [ ] Lint rule (ESLint import restriction, or dependency-cruiser config) prevents anything under `src/domain/**` from importing `react-native`, `expo*`, `expo-sqlite`, or `react-native-ble-*` (§15.1) — rule commits with at least one passing and one failing fixture.
- [ ] `package.json` scripts include `typecheck`, `lint`, `test`, and `start`.
- [ ] `README.md` at repo root describes how to install, prebuild, and run the dev build.

## Non-goals

- No BLE code, no real screens beyond placeholders.
- No SQLite schema — that is Phase 1 / storage work.

## Notes

- References: §16, §15.1, §23 Story 1, §22 Phase 0 task 6, R5.
- Depends on M02-01.
- Blocks M02-03, M02-06, M02-08.

issues.title: Configure expo-dev-client, Android package id, and expo-build-properties
issues.body:
## Context

Sprint 1 Story 1 requires an installable native dev build (§23) and §11.2 requires a custom dev build rather than Expo Go. §22 Phase 0 task 7 asks for a custom development build and Android package ID.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `expo-dev-client` installed and the app's entry point uses it.
- [ ] Android package id set to a stable reverse-DNS value (recorded in `app.json` / `app.config.ts`) and documented in `docs/dev-setup.md`.
- [ ] `expo-build-properties` plugin configured with `compileSdkVersion`, `targetSdkVersion`, `minSdkVersion`, `ndkVersion`, and `newArchEnabled` matching the stack locked by M02-01.
- [ ] Android manifest declares `BLUETOOTH_SCAN` and `BLUETOOTH_CONNECT` per §11.3 / R7 (runtime request flow is Phase 1 Story 2 — not this issue).
- [ ] `neverForLocation` NOT asserted yet — §11.3 forbids it until tested with these trackers.
- [ ] `expo prebuild` succeeds locally and the generated `android/` project is either committed or excluded intentionally (decision recorded in `docs/dev-setup.md`).

## Non-goals

- No runtime permission UI — that is Phase 1 Story 2.
- No BLE plugin wiring beyond what the locked stack requires.

## Notes

- References: §11.2, §11.3, §22 Phase 0 task 7, §23 Story 1, R6, R7, R9.
- Depends on M02-01, M02-02.
- Blocks M02-05.

issues.title: Install Android SDK components required by the locked BLE stack
issues.body:
## Context

The workstation currently has only android-35, build-tools 34.0.0, and NDK 27.2 installed. The stack locked by M02-01 may require different platform, build-tools, or NDK versions (Expo SDK 57 defaults differ from SDK 54). This task closes the gap so `expo prebuild` and the gradle build produce a matching APK. Raised to P0 because M02-05 (the Story 1 install/launch DoD) cannot build without these components.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Required SDK platform, build-tools, platform-tools, and NDK versions read from the M02-01 decision doc and listed in `docs/dev-setup.md`.
- [ ] Missing components installed via `sdkmanager` and the exact command lines committed to `docs/dev-setup.md`.
- [ ] `sdkmanager --list_installed` output pasted or referenced in `docs/dev-setup.md` after install.
- [ ] Gradle build of the scaffold from M02-02 + M02-03 succeeds locally without downloading additional components at build time.

## Non-goals

- No changes to global Windows PATH — installs stay under the existing Android SDK root.
- No CI runner provisioning — that is M02-08.

## Notes

- References: §11.2, §22 Phase 0 task 7.
- Depends on M02-01, M02-03.
- Blocks M02-05.

issues.title: Build and install the dev build over USB and verify launch without Metro
issues.body:
## Context

Sprint 1 Story 1 acceptance criteria (§23) require the app to install by USB and launch without Metro in a release-like test build. §22 Phase 0 task 8 requires `adb devices` verification. This is the first end-to-end proof that a Phase 1 build cycle will work.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `adb devices` lists the tablet as authorized, and the command is documented in `docs/dev-setup.md`.
- [ ] `eas build --profile development --platform android` (or the equivalent local `expo run:android --variant release`) produces an installable APK.
- [ ] APK installs on the tablet over USB and the app launches to the placeholder home screen.
- [ ] A second APK built in a release-like profile launches on the tablet without Metro running (no dev server) and does not crash within 60 s (§23 Story 1 AC 3).
- [ ] Repository documents the exact build + install commands and the pinned dependency versions (§23 Story 1 AC 4) in `docs/dev-setup.md`.

## Non-goals

- No BLE runtime code — placeholder screens only.
- No signed release keystore — that is Phase 7.

## Notes

- References: §23 Story 1, §22 Phase 0 task 8, §11.2.
- Hardware required: tablet + USB cable.
- Depends on M02-02, M02-03, M02-04.
- Blocks M02-07 and Phase 1.

issues.title: Add build-info screen showing app, OS, and dependency versions
issues.body:
## Context

§22 Phase 0 task 9 and §23 Story 1 AC 2 require the app to show build/version information. §16 places this at `src/diagnostics/buildInfo.ts`. This screen also becomes the diagnostic surface later phases lean on when reporting issues.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `src/diagnostics/buildInfo.ts` exposes a pure function returning app name, app version, build number, git commit short SHA (baked at build time), Expo SDK version, RN version, and BLE library name + version.
- [ ] A Build Info screen renders those values plus Android release, API level, device model, and locale using `expo-device` / `expo-application` / `expo-localization` (any RN/Expo imports live in the screen, not in `buildInfo.ts` domain surface — §15.1).
- [ ] The screen is reachable from a settings or diagnostics entry visible in the tab skeleton.
- [ ] Values render correctly on the tablet in a build produced by M02-05.
- [ ] Unit test covers `buildInfo.ts` for the pure fields.

## Non-goals

- No log export UI — logging is §20.4 / later phases.
- No BLE state on this screen — that is Phase 1.

## Notes

- References: §22 Phase 0 task 9, §23 Story 1, §16 (`src/diagnostics/buildInfo.ts`), §15.1.
- Depends on M02-02.
- Consumed by M02-05 verification and future Phase 7 release checklist.

issues.title: Archive the known-good APK and lockfile as the Phase 0 baseline artifact

issues.title: Add CI pipeline running typecheck, lint, and unit tests
issues.body:
## Context

§21.1 requires unit tests on domain logic and §15.1 forbids domain code from importing RN/Expo/SQLite/BLE — CI is where that boundary rule keeps being enforced. Phase 0 DoD does not require a full device build in CI, only that the repo can guard basic invariants.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] GitHub Actions (or the project's chosen CI) workflow runs on push and pull request against the default branch.
- [ ] Workflow runs `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` (or the equivalent), then `typecheck`, `lint`, and `test` scripts defined in M02-02.
- [ ] The dependency-cruiser / ESLint import-restriction rule from M02-02 fails the build if `src/domain/**` imports RN/Expo/SQLite/BLE.
- [ ] A minimal placeholder unit test (e.g. `buildInfo.test.ts` from M02-06) is present and green.
- [ ] README badge or link points to the workflow.
- [ ] Workflow does NOT attempt an Android build — that stays a local step for Phase 0.

## Non-goals

- No Android emulator or device farm.
- No Detox / e2e tests — those are §21.5, later phases.
- No release automation.

## Notes

- References: §21.1, §15.1, §16.
- Depends on M02-02, M02-06.

epic.title: [EPIC] Phase 1 — Velocity Lab Bluetooth listener
epic.body:
## Objectives

- Connect to one physical tracker.
- Inventory GATT services, characteristics, and descriptors.
- Subscribe to notify/indicate characteristics and capture raw frames.
- Export diagnostics captures for offline analysis on Windows.
- Prove two trackers can remain connected concurrently.

## Milestones

- M03 — BLE permissions & Bluetooth-state onboarding
- M04 — Bounded scan & advertisement capture
- M05 — Single-tracker connect & GATT inventory
- M06 — Notification subscription & raw-frame persistence
- M07 — Observation markers & JSON capture export
- M08 — Disconnect / reconnect resilience
- M09 — Dual-tracker concurrent connections
- M10 — First repeatable punch frame captured (go/no-go)

## Definition of done

- A single known punch can be associated with a repeatable raw notification from one tracker.
- Both trackers can remain connected concurrently.
- Every notification is persisted as a `RawBleFrame` (base64 + hex + monotonic timestamp) before any decoding.
- The Velocity Lab listener workspace renders throttled to 5–10 Hz and surfaces the DB write-backlog when persistence falls behind.
- No writes are issued to unknown GATT characteristics except through an explicit developer-mode confirmation.
- JSON capture export includes frames, markers, GATT inventory, and device fingerprints and can be transferred to Windows for Wireshark correlation.

## Non-goals

- Decoding punch-event semantics or velocity fields (Phase 2).
- Calibration profiles (Phase 3).
- punchCraft or Puncheokie session UIs.
- Spotify or any network integration.
- Simplified end-user mode; Velocity Lab remains a diagnostic surface.

## Sub-issues

GitHub auto-populates this list from linked sub-issues; do not edit by hand.

issues.title: Request and explain BLE permissions on first launch
issues.body:
## Context

Sprint 1 Story 2 (spec §23). Phase 1 / M03. First functional slice of the Velocity Lab onboarding flow: the app must ask for the Bluetooth permissions it needs, explain why, and gracefully handle denial or Bluetooth-off states. Covers spec §11.3 (permission policy) and §7.1 (Velocity Lab responsibilities: Bluetooth permission onboarding).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] First launch explains why Bluetooth access is needed before the OS prompt fires.
- [ ] Denied permission produces a recoverable UI with a retry affordance.
- [ ] Permanently denied permission links out to the Android app settings page.
- [ ] Bluetooth-off state is distinguishable from permission denial in the UI copy and iconography.
- [ ] Rationale copy avoids `impact speed`, `force`, `power`, `energy`; use `tracker-reported velocity` (§4.3).

## Non-goals

- Scanning or connecting to any device.
- Background/foreground permission handling (§11.11 — later).

## Notes

Wires up `src/ble/PermissionService.ts` behind `src/ble/BleManagerFacade.ts` (§11.4, §16). React components must never call `react-native-ble-plx` directly. Requires the tablet for verification of all four states.

issues.title: Implement PermissionService with API-level branching
issues.body:
## Context

M03 / Phase 1. Implements the runtime permission branching required by spec §11.3: Android 12/API 31+ uses `BLUETOOTH_SCAN` and `BLUETOOTH_CONNECT`; older Android versions fall back to the required location permission for BLE scanning.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `src/ble/PermissionService.ts` exposes `requestBleAccess()` returning a discriminated result (granted / denied / permanentlyDenied / bluetoothOff).
- [ ] Branch selection is driven by `Platform.Version` and covered by unit tests using a mockable platform accessor.
- [ ] Service does not import Expo/RN modules from domain code (§15.1).
- [ ] AndroidManifest declares SCAN/CONNECT for API 31+ and the legacy scan permission for lower API levels.

## Non-goals

- The `neverForLocation` assertion — tracked separately in M03-05.
- iOS permission handling.

## Notes

See references R7–R9 in spec §11.3. Depends on Phase 0 dev-build being installable.

issues.title: Detect Bluetooth adapter state and surface remediation UI
issues.body:
## Context

Spec §11.3 requires a user-facing remediation screen when Bluetooth is disabled. This task adds adapter-state observation and the corresponding UI hook so downstream scan/connect flows can precondition on `bluetoothOn`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Adapter state is observed via the BLE facade and re-emitted through a Zustand store slice.
- [ ] Velocity Lab dashboard blocks scan/connect actions while adapter is off and shows a `Turn on Bluetooth` remediation card.
- [ ] State transitions (on→off, off→on) update the UI within one adapter callback without a manual refresh.
- [ ] Copy is distinct from permission-denied copy (M03-04).

## Non-goals

- Programmatically toggling Bluetooth from the app.

## Notes

Adapter observer lives in `src/ble/BleManagerFacade.ts`; UI wiring in `src/app/velocity-lab` route + `src/state/useDeviceStore.ts` (§16).

issues.title: Handle denied and permanently-denied permission recovery paths
issues.body:
## Context

Completes the recoverable-denial requirement of Story 2 (§23) and §11.3. Ensures the user always has a next action when permissions are refused.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Soft-denied state exposes a `Try again` button that re-invokes the OS prompt.
- [ ] Permanently-denied state exposes an `Open Android settings` action using an Intent that deep-links to this app's settings page.
- [ ] Returning from settings re-checks permissions and updates state without an app restart.
- [ ] Distinct copy for SCAN vs CONNECT denial on API 31+.

## Non-goals

- Analytics or telemetry on denial reasons.

## Notes

Build on `PermissionService` from M03-02. Verify all three states on the test tablet.

issues.title: Decide neverForLocation assertion via on-device test
issues.body:
## Context

Spec §11.3 says `neverForLocation` shall only be enabled after testing confirms it does not filter these trackers on the target OS/device. This is a policy decision gated by a physical test on the tablet with both v1 trackers powered on and advertising.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] On-device test procedure documented in `docs/ble-neverforlocation-test.md` (scenario, tablet OS build, both tracker IDs).
- [ ] Test executed on the target tablet with both trackers powered; result recorded (advertisements observed with vs. without the assertion).
- [ ] AndroidManifest reflects the decision (assertion on or off) with an inline comment linking to the test doc.
- [ ] If disabled, ADR captures the reason; if enabled, test log is attached to the issue.

## Non-goals

- Broader location-permission UX changes.

## Notes

Hardware required. Blocks M04 scanning tuning if the assertion turns out to filter our trackers.

issues.title: Wire permission rationale into first-launch onboarding flow
issues.body:
## Context

Sprint 1 Story 2 explicitly requires that first launch explains why Bluetooth is needed. This task adds the onboarding route and ensures the rationale is only shown once per install, but re-shown after a permanent denial recovery.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] New Expo Router screen under `src/app/onboarding/ble-rationale.tsx` shown once at first launch before any scan.
- [ ] Persisted flag in AsyncStorage prevents repeat display after grant.
- [ ] Screen offers `Continue` (invokes PermissionService) and `Not now` (routes back to dashboard read-only).
- [ ] Copy references `tracker-reported velocity`, never `force`/`power`/`energy` (§4.3).

## Non-goals

- General app tour.

## Notes

Depends on M03-02.

issues.title: Scan and capture advertisements
issues.body:
## Context

Sprint 1 Story 3 (§23). Phase 1 / M04. Vertical slice: the user starts a bounded scan and every discovered advertisement is captured with enough metadata that we can identify our trackers and reproduce results in Wireshark. Implements spec §11.6 scanning strategy and feeds §12.2 capture workflow.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Scan runs for a bounded interval (default 10–15 seconds; §11.6).
- [ ] Each result records device ID, name, RSSI, service UUIDs, manufacturer data, and timestamp.
- [ ] Duplicate advertisements are summarized without losing the latest values.
- [ ] Results can be exported (JSON).
- [ ] Scan cannot run indefinitely; explicit start/stop with a visible countdown.
- [ ] React components call the facade, never `react-native-ble-plx` directly (§11.4).

## Non-goals

- Filtering by known service UUID (deferred until identifiers are confirmed — §11.6).
- Connecting to any discovered device.

## Notes

Implement `src/ble/TrackerScanner.ts` behind `BleManagerFacade` (§16). Hardware required to observe real v1 tracker advertisements.

issues.title: Implement TrackerScanner with bounded scan lifecycle
issues.body:
## Context

M04 / Phase 1. Core scan primitive backing Story 3 (§23) and §11.6. Must never loop endlessly and must cleanly stop when the caller cancels or the timeout elapses.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `src/ble/TrackerScanner.ts` exposes `start({ durationMs })` returning an `AsyncIterable<AdvertisementSnapshot>` plus `stop()`.
- [ ] Timeouts fire even if consumers stop reading.
- [ ] Scan is idempotent — a second start while running rejects rather than double-scanning.
- [ ] Unit tests cover cancellation, timeout, and duplicate-start rejection with a mocked BLE library.

## Non-goals

- UI wiring (M04-01).

## Notes

See spec §11.6 references R10 for battery-cost warning.

issues.title: Define AdvertisementSnapshot record and capture pipeline
issues.body:
## Context

Required shape for Story 3 acceptance criteria (§23). Captures every field we need for §11.7 fingerprinting and later `scoreAdvertisement` (§12.3).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `AdvertisementSnapshot` type in `src/ble/bleTypes.ts` includes device id, name, RSSI, service UUID list, manufacturer data map, monotonic timestamp, wall-clock ISO.
- [ ] Each advertisement is written to an in-memory ring for the UI and to storage-backed capture rows.
- [ ] Timestamps use the same monotonic clock later used for `RawBleFrame` (§12.4).

## Non-goals

- Persistent fingerprint diffing (later, M05 device identity).

## Notes

Domain types must not import RN/Expo modules (§15.1).

issues.title: Summarize duplicate advertisements without losing latest values
issues.body:
## Context

Story 3 AC (§23): duplicates must be collapsed without dropping the freshest values.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] UI shows one row per device with `seenCount`, `lastRssi`, and `lastSeenAt`.
- [ ] Underlying capture table still records every advertisement for offline analysis.
- [ ] Sort order stable when RSSI ties.
- [ ] Unit tests over a synthetic stream of 500 advertisements from three devices.
- [ ] Dedup key is `androidDeviceId + hash(advPayload)` within a 1-second window; the latest RSSI and `lastSeenAt` always overwrite prior summary values (§11.6, §11.7).

## Non-goals

- Historical charts.

## Notes

Implementation lives in the scan store (`src/state/useDeviceStore.ts` scan slice).

issues.title: Export scan results as JSON
issues.body:
## Context

Story 3 AC (§23) requires exporting scan results. This feeds §12.2 workflow (analysis on Windows).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `Export` action in the scan UI produces a JSON file containing every captured advertisement, not just the summary.
- [ ] Schema is versioned (`schemaVersion` field) and documented in `docs/exports/scan-schema.md`.
- [ ] Export honors the same monotonic clock and includes app + OS version.
- [ ] File is written to a share-sheet compatible location on Android.

## Non-goals

- Cloud upload.

## Notes

Shares the exporter foundation with M07 capture export.

issues.title: Connect and inventory one tracker
issues.body:
## Context

Sprint 1 Story 4 (§23). Phase 1 / M05. Vertical slice bringing a single tracker from a scan result to a fully-inventoried GATT server, with the inventory persisted for offline reference (§17.1). Implements §11.5 state machine happy path and §11.9 discovery.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] User selects the tracker from the scan list.
- [ ] Connection state (connecting/bonding/discovering/initializing/ready) is visible in the dashboard card.
- [ ] Service discovery completes; every service, characteristic, and property is displayed in the GATT inspector.
- [ ] Inventory is persisted in `gatt_inventory` (M05-04 migration).
- [ ] Normal disconnect closes resources cleanly (no leaked subscriptions or handles).
- [ ] No writes are issued to unknown characteristics (§12.1, §7.2C).

## Non-goals

- Subscribing to notifications (M06).
- Two-tracker aggregate (M09).

## Notes

Wires `TrackerConnection` behind `BleManagerFacade` (§11.4, §16). Hardware required.

issues.title: Build BleManagerFacade and TrackerConnection skeleton
issues.body:
## Context

M05 / Phase 1. Implements the component boundary defined in §11.4: a single facade behind which every BLE call lives, and one `TrackerConnection` per physical device driving the §11.5 state machine.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `src/ble/BleManagerFacade.ts` is the only module importing `react-native-ble-plx`.
- [ ] `src/ble/TrackerConnection.ts` exposes `connect`, `disconnect`, `state$`, and `connectionGeneration`.
- [ ] State transitions match §11.5 and are unit-testable via injected fakes.
- [ ] Grep guard (lint rule or test) fails the build if any file outside `src/ble/` imports `react-native-ble-plx`.

## Non-goals

- GATT operation serialization (M05-03).
- Reconnection policy (M08).

## Notes

Per §15.1, domain modules must not depend on RN/Expo/BLE.

issues.title: Implement GattOperationQueue with per-connection serialization
issues.body:
## Context

Spec §11.8: Android BLE stacks misbehave when operations overlap. Every read/write/descriptor/MTU call for one connection must serialize through a queue with id, type, timeout, retry policy, expected callback, and diagnostic log.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `src/ble/GattOperationQueue.ts` serializes operations per `connectionGeneration` while allowing parallel queues across trackers.
- [ ] Every enqueued op has id, type, timeout, retry policy, expected-callback shape, and completion/error timestamp.
- [ ] Timeouts surface as typed errors, not thrown strings.
- [ ] Unit tests cover ordering, timeout, retry, and interleaving of two connections.

## Non-goals

- Adaptive backoff (M08).

## Notes

Used by M05 discovery and M06 subscription flows.

issues.title: SQLite migration for tracker_devices, ble_captures, ble_frames, gatt_inventory
issues.body:
## Context

Spec §17.1 defines `tracker_devices`, `ble_captures`, `ble_frames`; Phase 1 adds a `gatt_inventory` table so discovery results are inspectable offline. WAL journal mode and foreign keys are non-negotiable per project conventions.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] New migration under `src/storage/migrations/` creates `tracker_devices`, `ble_captures`, `ble_frames`, `gatt_inventory` with columns matching §17.1 (plus `gatt_inventory` fields: service_uuid, characteristic_uuid, properties, descriptors_json, device_id FK, discovered_at).
- [ ] `PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL` and `PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON` applied at database open.
- [ ] Indices on `ble_frames(capture_id, monotonic_time_ms)` and `gatt_inventory(device_id)`.
- [ ] Migration is idempotent and covered by a boot-time test.

## Non-goals

- Calibration, session, program tables (later phases).

## Notes

Repositories in `src/storage/repositories/` are updated in follow-up tasks; this issue only lands schema + boot pragmas.

issues.title: Persist GATT inventory rows from discovery
issues.body:
## Context

Spec §7.2C GATT inspector must display persisted inventory; Story 4 requires that every discovered service/characteristic is persisted.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `CaptureRepository` (or new `GattInventoryRepository`) writes one row per characteristic on discovery completion.
- [ ] Re-discovery upserts rather than duplicates.
- [ ] Inspector UI reads from storage so inventory survives app restart.
- [ ] Rows include `properties` array and descriptor UUIDs.

## Non-goals

- Diffing across firmware revisions.

## Notes

Depends on M05-04.

issues.title: Build GATT inspector UI listing services, characteristics, descriptors
issues.body:
## Context

Spec §7.2C. Presents the inventory required by Story 4 AC and prepares the ground for M06 subscription selection.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Route under `src/app/velocity-lab/gatt.tsx` renders services with expandable characteristic rows.
- [ ] Each row shows UUID, standard name (if known), properties (read/write/writeWithoutResponse/notify/indicate), and descriptors.
- [ ] Unknown characteristics render a warning badge and disable any write control (§12.1, §7.2C).
- [ ] Values are only shown for characteristics with the `read` property and only when the user taps `Read`.

## Non-goals

- Write templates (later, developer mode only).

## Notes

Component lives in `src/components/`; page in `src/app/velocity-lab/` (§16).

issues.title: Investigate FightCamp v1 bonding behavior on the target tablet
issues.body:
## Context

Spec §11.10: bonding may be implicit, prompted, or require an explicit native module. This spike determines which path applies to the v1 trackers on the target Android build so M05 and later phases can commit to a policy.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Document under `docs/spikes/ble-bonding.md` records: does connect succeed without bond? Does any protected op trigger an OS bond prompt? Does `react-native-ble-plx` expose bond state reliably?
- [ ] Decision recorded: `no bond`, `library-managed`, or `custom Expo native module required` (per §11.10 fallback list).
- [ ] If a native module is chosen, a follow-up task is filed under a later phase referencing the four required surfaces (create bond, current state, event subscription, dev-mode remove).
- [ ] Time-boxed to 1 working day.

## Non-goals

- Building the native module in this issue.

## Notes

Hardware required. Two trackers plus tablet. Deliverable is a decision, not code.

issues.title: Subscribe and persist raw notifications
issues.body:
## Context

Sprint 1 Story 5 (§23). Phase 1 / M06. Vertical slice: with a tracker connected, subscribe to notify/indicate characteristics and persist every incoming frame as a `RawBleFrame` (§12.4) before any parsing (§11.9 step 5). Feeds the listener workspace UI (§7.2B).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] App subscribes to selected notify/indicate characteristics.
- [ ] Every callback receives a monotonic timestamp.
- [ ] Payload is preserved as Base64 and hex.
- [ ] Raw frame is stored before protocol parsing.
- [ ] Listener UI shows a bounded recent-frame list.
- [ ] Database backlog is visible if writes fall behind.
- [ ] Listener UI updates throttled to 5–10 Hz regardless of notification rate (§7.2B).

## Non-goals

- Decoding punch events (Phase 2).
- Markers/export (M07).

## Notes

Wires `NotificationRouter` and `BleCaptureSink` (§11.4). Hardware required.

issues.title: Implement NotificationRouter over notify/indicate characteristics
issues.body:
## Context

Spec §11.9. After discovery the router identifies all notify/indicate characteristics, subscribes according to policy, records the subscription op result, persists every incoming frame, and forwards it to the adapter registry (adapter no-op in Phase 1).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `src/ble/NotificationRouter.ts` subscribes to a caller-selected set (default: all safe notify/indicate) via `GattOperationQueue`.
- [ ] Subscription success/failure per characteristic is persisted with the capture.
- [ ] Unsubscribe on disconnect leaves no dangling handlers.
- [ ] Unit tests cover subscribe-all, subscribe-subset, and error paths.

## Non-goals

- Adapter selection (Phase 2).

## Notes

Must route via facade; components never touch the router directly (§11.4).

issues.title: Persist RawBleFrame via BleCaptureSink before any parsing
issues.body:
## Context

Spec §12.4 defines the immutable raw-frame contract; §12.1 mandates that raw captures stay immutable and §11.9 that every frame is persisted before parsing.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `src/capture/BleCaptureService.ts` implements a `BleCaptureSink` that receives frames from the router and writes them to `ble_frames`.
- [ ] Every row includes id, capture_id, device_id, monotonic_time_ms, wall_time_iso, direction, service_uuid, characteristic_uuid, value_base64, value_hex, connection_generation.
- [ ] Writes are batched (e.g., 50 rows or 100 ms whichever first) to keep up with burst rates without blocking the notification callback.
- [ ] No decoder runs before the frame is durably written; a test asserts the ordering with a spy adapter.
- [ ] `NotificationRouter` MUST hand the frame to `BleCaptureSink` and await enqueue (in-memory acknowledgment is sufficient; durable batch flush follows) before any downstream decode, inspection, or UI-projection path is invoked; a unit test with a spy decoder asserts the sink call happens strictly before any decoder or listener callback (§11.9 step 5, §12.1, §12.4).

## Non-goals

- Decoded event persistence (Phase 2).

## Notes

Depends on M05-04 migration.

issues.title: Build listener workspace UI with throttled render and backlog indicator
issues.body:
## Context

Spec §7.2B lists the listener workspace surface: elapsed time, per-hand counters, latest parsed event (placeholder in Phase 1), latest raw payload hex, service/characteristic UUID, receive timestamp, notification rate, duplicate count, sequence-gap count, error count, dropped-frame warning, capture recording status. The UI must throttle to 5–10 Hz and expose the DB write-backlog per Phase 1 rules.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Route `src/app/velocity-lab/listener.tsx` renders the fields above using a `RawFrameList` component (§16).
- [ ] Renders coalesce updates to 5–10 Hz (measure with performance markers in a test build).
- [ ] A visible `DB backlog: N frames` indicator turns amber above a configurable threshold and red when the sink cannot keep up.
- [ ] Copy uses `tracker-reported velocity` where applicable and never `force`/`power`/`energy` (§4.3).

## Non-goals

- Filters (deferred), replay (Phase 2), guarded writes (M06-05).

## Notes

Depends on M06-02, M06-03. Area is `ble` because the listener workspace is the primary Phase 1 M06 surface and the phase-area rule pins M06=ble; the route file lives under `src/app/velocity-lab/` per §16 but the owning subsystem is BLE capture.

issues.title: Enforce no writes to unknown GATT characteristics outside developer mode
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 1 rule and spec §12.1 / §7.2C: unknown characteristics never receive arbitrary writes. Any write must be behind a known command template or an explicit developer-mode confirmation. This issue implements the guardrail end-to-end.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `GattOperationQueue` rejects write ops targeting characteristics not present in an approved-writes registry unless a `developerModeConfirmed: true` flag is set on the op.
- [ ] The registry is empty in Phase 1 — every write must therefore be dev-mode-gated.
- [ ] Developer mode is off by default and gated by a hidden toggle under Settings; enabling it shows a persistent banner on the listener and inspector screens.
- [ ] GATT inspector write controls are disabled for unknown characteristics and require an explicit `I understand this may brick the tracker` confirm dialog when developer mode is on (UI acceptance criterion).
- [ ] Unit tests cover: reject unknown write without flag; allow with flag; still reject if flag set but developer mode is off in state.
- [ ] GATT inspector write control in `src/app/velocity-lab/gatt.tsx` is disabled unless developer mode is enabled AND the target characteristic is on the known-writable allowlist; attempted writes to unknown characteristics show an inline `Blocked: unknown characteristic (§12.1)` message and are logged to the diagnostics log with the characteristic UUID and timestamp (§7.2C).

## Non-goals

- Populating the approved-writes registry (Phase 2, after initialization writes are observed).

## Notes

See §12.1 safety rules — observe before writing.

issues.title: Wire notification-rate, duplicate, gap, and error counters
issues.body:
## Context

Listener workspace fields per §7.2B. Counters live next to the raw-frame stream and feed the UI throttled at 5–10 Hz.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Per-characteristic notification rate (rolling 1 s window) computed in the capture layer.
- [ ] Duplicate detection (identical payload within N ms window) increments a counter without discarding rows.
- [ ] Sequence gap counter is a placeholder that reads from a pluggable `SequenceProbe` (Phase 2 fills it in).
- [ ] Error counter increments on subscription errors and callback exceptions.

## Non-goals

- True protocol-level dedup (Phase 2, §12.6).

## Notes

Expose counters via `useDeviceStore` for the listener UI.

issues.title: Mark controlled observations during a listener session
issues.body:
## Context

Sprint 1 Story 6 (§23). Phase 1 / M07. Vertical slice: while the listener is running, the user can tap `Mark` and attach a label (e.g., `one-left-jab`) so Windows-side analysis can correlate labels with nearby frames (§12.2).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] User can tap `Mark` and enter or select a label.
- [ ] Marker has the same monotonic time base as frames (§12.4 clock).
- [ ] Export includes markers.
- [ ] Windows analysis process can correlate a marker with nearby frames.
- [ ] Common labels available as one-tap presets: `no-punch`, `one-left`, `one-right`, `alternating-5`.

## Non-goals

- Marker editing after capture close (later).
- Auto-marking from decoded events (Phase 2).

## Notes

Depends on M06 capture pipeline. Hardware recommended for realistic timing.

issues.title: Add marker entry UI with label presets and free-form input
issues.body:
## Context

UI slice for Story 6 (§23) inside the listener workspace (§7.2B).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `Mark` button visible in the listener toolbar during capture.
- [ ] Preset chips: `no-punch`, `one-left`, `one-right`, `alt-5`, plus `Custom…`.
- [ ] Custom label validated: 1–32 chars, `[a-z0-9-]`.
- [ ] Marker action never blocks the notification callback path.

## Non-goals

- Editing existing markers.

## Notes

Component under `src/components/`; page updates `src/app/velocity-lab/listener.tsx`.

issues.title: Persist markers with monotonic timestamp against the active capture
issues.body:
## Context

Story 6 AC (§23) — markers must share the frame clock so correlation is unambiguous.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] New `ble_capture_markers` table (columns: id, capture_id FK, label, monotonic_time_ms, wall_time_iso, author=`user`).
- [ ] Insert path uses the same monotonic clock source used by `BleCaptureSink` (M06-03).
- [ ] `CaptureRepository.addMarker` covered by unit tests.
- [ ] Migration is idempotent and additive over M05-04.

## Non-goals

- Auto-generated markers.

## Notes

Coordinate with M05-04 migration numbering.

issues.title: Export capture as JSON including frames, markers, GATT inventory, and device fingerprints
issues.body:
## Context

Story 6 export requirement plus §12.2 workflow (transfer to Windows for Wireshark correlation). Establishes the versioned capture-export format used by future phases. The Phase 1 epic Definition of Done explicitly requires device fingerprints in the export.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `src/capture/CaptureExporter.ts` produces a JSON document with `schemaVersion`, `app`, `os`, `capture`, `device`, `gattInventory[]`, `frames[]`, `markers[]`, and `deviceFingerprint`.
- [ ] `deviceFingerprint` includes every §11.7 identity field available: android device id (as observed by the library), advertisement name, service UUID set, manufacturer-specific data, serial-number characteristic if read, firmware/hardware revision if read, LED/hand assignment, and protocol-adapter confidence.
- [ ] Frames are ordered by `monotonic_time_ms`; hex and base64 both present per §12.4.
- [ ] Schema is documented at `docs/exports/capture-schema.md` including the `deviceFingerprint` sub-schema.
- [ ] Export of a 10-minute capture completes in under 10 seconds on the target tablet.

## Non-goals

- Compression (deferred).
- Decoded events (Phase 2).

## Notes

Shares JSON foundation with M04-05.

issues.title: Share exported capture via Android share sheet
issues.body:
## Context

Enables the Windows-side workflow (§12.2 step 6). Complements M07-04 by getting the file out of the app sandbox.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `Share` action on a capture opens the Android share sheet with the JSON file attached.
- [ ] Filename encodes capture id + start timestamp.
- [ ] Works with USB file-transfer and email targets on the target tablet.
- [ ] Failed shares surface an error toast, not a silent no-op.

## Non-goals

- Cloud upload integrations.

## Notes

Hardware verification required.

issues.title: Implement RawBleFrame and capture-file retention policy
issues.body:
## Context

Spec §17.2 data-retention rules: general raw diagnostic captures are kept for 30 days or a user-configured storage ceiling; users may pin a capture to exempt it from cleanup; storage usage must be visible in Settings. No existing Phase 1 issue enforces this, and unmanaged `ble_frames` growth will exhaust device storage during protocol discovery.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `src/capture/RetentionService.ts` (or equivalent in `src/storage/`) purges `ble_captures`, `ble_frames`, `ble_capture_markers`, and exported JSON files that are older than 30 days and are not pinned, and additionally trims oldest-first when total capture storage exceeds a user-configured ceiling (default 500 MB).
- [ ] `ble_captures` gains a `pinned` boolean column via an additive migration; a `Pin capture` action is exposed in the captures list UI (§7.1 capture export selection surface).
- [ ] Retention pass runs at app start and on a manual `Run cleanup now` action in Settings; unit tests cover age-based purge, ceiling-based trim, and pin exemption.
- [ ] Settings screen displays current capture storage usage (bytes) and the configured ceiling; changing the ceiling is persisted and re-evaluated immediately.
- [ ] Pinned calibration captures and session-linked captures are never purged, per §17.2 retention classes.
- [ ] User-initiated `Delete all diagnostic captures` action is available and confirms before executing.

## Non-goals

- Cloud archival before purge.
- Automatic pinning heuristics.

## Notes

Depends on M05-04 (schema) and M07-04 (exported file layout). Aligns with §17.2 retention classes: session events indefinite, calibration captures indefinite while referenced, general captures time/size bounded.

issues.title: Recover from unexpected disconnects with bounded reconnect
issues.body:
## Context

Sprint 1 recovery slice mapped to M08 (Phase 1). Implements §19.3 reconnection target and the `recovering` states of §11.5 without any decoded-event dependency.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Disconnect detected immediately through the BLE callback (§19.3).
- [ ] Connection enters `recovering` state and UI reflects it distinctly from `dormant`.
- [ ] Bounded reconnect attempts with exponential backoff and a total budget; budget exhausted transitions to `error` with a `Retry` action.
- [ ] Notification subscriptions are restored on successful reconnect (§19.3).
- [ ] Frames captured after reconnect carry a new `connection_generation` per §12.4.

## Non-goals

- Offline sync of missed events (Phase 2).
- Session-completeness degradation UI (later).

## Notes

Builds on M05 connection and M06 subscription paths. Hardware required (turn tracker off/on).

issues.title: Detect disconnects and transition connection to recovering
issues.body:
## Context

Part of §19.3 and §11.5. Ensures the state machine doesn't get stuck when the tracker vanishes.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `TrackerConnection` listens for BLE disconnect callbacks and enters `recovering` within one event loop turn.
- [ ] `connectionGeneration` increments on transition out of `ready`/`streaming`.
- [ ] Store slice notifies UI observers.
- [ ] Unit test with a fake BLE library covers the transition.

## Non-goals

- Reconnect attempts (M08-03).

## Notes

Extends `src/ble/TrackerConnection.ts` (§16).

issues.title: Implement bounded reconnect with exponential backoff
issues.body:
## Context

§19.3 requires bounded reconnects with backoff.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Backoff schedule (e.g., 500ms, 1s, 2s, 5s, 10s, cap 10s) configurable in one place.
- [ ] Retry budget default 6 attempts, then transitions to `error`.
- [ ] Attempt counter resets on successful `streaming` re-entry.
- [ ] Manual `Reconnect` from UI bypasses backoff and resets the budget.
- [ ] Deterministic tests using a fake clock.

## Non-goals

- Global reconnect coordinator across trackers (§11.4 keeps them independent).

## Notes

Depends on M08-02.

issues.title: Restore notification subscriptions after reconnect
issues.body:
## Context

§19.3 explicitly requires restored subscriptions. The router owns the desired-subscription set; on reconnect it must re-issue subscribes without a user round-trip.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `NotificationRouter` retains the desired subscription set across connection generations.
- [ ] On successful reconnect + rediscovery, the router re-subscribes in the previously used order.
- [ ] Restore failure per-characteristic is logged and increments the listener error counter (M06-06).
- [ ] Integration test using paired mock BLE + router harness.
- [ ] Reconnect resumes writing frames into the SAME active `ble_captures` row rather than opening a new capture; a synthetic gap-marker row (label=`reconnect-gap`, monotonic timestamps for disconnect and reconnect) is inserted into `ble_capture_markers` so downstream analysis can see the discontinuity (§12.4 `connection_generation` increments while capture id stays stable).

## Non-goals

- Offline sync commands (Phase 2, §12.3).

## Notes

Extends M06-02.

issues.title: Surface degraded state when reconnect budget is exhausted
issues.body:
## Context

epic.title: [EPIC] Phase 2 — Protocol initialization, decoding, and synchronization
epic.body:
## Objectives

- Reproduce the required official initialization sequence for FightCamp v1 trackers using only observed writes.
- Decode punch events into deterministic `TrackerPunchEvent` records.
- Prove deduplication and offline-recovery behavior against replay fixtures.

## Milestones

- M11 — Initialization plan from observed traffic
- M12 — FightCampV1Adapter skeleton & device status decoding
- M13 — Punch-event decoding: boundaries, hand, sequence, timestamp
- M14 — Velocity & punch-type field analysis, capability detection
- M15 — Session start/stop, offline sync, dedup & gap handling
- M16 — Replay harness & fixture test suite

## Definition of done

- The app generates a deterministic `TrackerPunchEvent` for controlled left and right punches.
- The app does not double-count replayed events (dedup verified via replay harness).
- Unsupported fields are documented and surfaced via capability detection.
- All velocity display uses the phrase "tracker units" until validated (§4.3) — enforced by an executable lint/test.
- Every confirmed capture from Phase 1 exists as a replay fixture that runs in CI without BLE hardware.
- A UUID allowlist prevents GATT writes to any characteristic not observed in official-app captures (§12.1).
- Every `TrackerPunchEvent` carries `decoderId` and `decoderVersion`, and replay fixtures pin expected output to a specific decoder version.
- `RawBleFrame.monotonicTimeMs` is stamped from a monotonic clock at ingest, independent of wall time.

## Non-goals

- No calibration transforms (Phase 3).
- No punchCraft session UI (Phase 4).
- No Puncheokie programs or Spotify (Phases 5–6).
- No writes to GATT characteristics whose meaning has not been observed in official-app traffic (§12.1).
- No claims that velocity is in physical units (m/s, mph) — see §4.3.

## Sub-issues

GitHub auto-populates this list from issues that reference this epic.

issues.title: Diff official-app GATT writes against Velocity Lab inventory
issues.body:
## Context

Part of Phase 2 / M11. Using the HCI snoop logs and Velocity Lab GATT inventory captured in Phase 1 (§12.2), compare initialization writes performed by the official FightCamp app to what our listener sees on connect. Establishes the evidence base for `buildInitializationPlan` (§12.3) and honors the observe-before-writing rule (§12.1).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] For each connected tracker, produce a written diff of GATT operations performed by the official app between connection and first punch notification.
- [ ] Diff distinguishes reads, notification subscriptions (CCCD writes), and characteristic writes with payload hex.
- [ ] Each writable characteristic is annotated with observed payload(s), frequency, and physical scenario that produced them.
- [ ] Result committed under `docs/protocol/init-diff.md` with links to source snoop logs.
- [ ] Any characteristic write that could not be attributed to a scenario is flagged as "do-not-replay" with rationale.
- [ ] Output enumerates the confirmed observed-writes UUID allowlist consumed by M11-04.

## Non-goals

- Do not implement the initialization plan here (M11-03).
- Do not attempt to decode payload semantics beyond byte-level annotation.

## Notes

- Inputs: Phase 1 Story 5/8 captures under `docs/protocol/captures/`.
- Reference §12.1 (safety), §12.2 (capture workflow), §11.4 (component boundaries).
- Purely analysis; no code touched.

issues.title: Confirm minimum initialization sequence for one tracker
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 2 / M11 spike. From the M11-01 diff, identify the minimum set of writes and subscriptions that must be issued after connect for the tracker to begin emitting punch notifications. This is the input to `buildInitializationPlan(ctx)` (§12.3) and must be justified per §12.1 (never guess packet meaning from one sample). This spike is the Phase 2 go/no-go gate for writing to real hardware.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Deliverable: a decision document `docs/protocol/init-plan.md` listing each operation, its evidence (capture ID + frame offset), and confidence tag.
- [ ] Each operation is reproduced at least three times across independent captures before being marked "required" (§12.2).
- [ ] Operations without triple-evidence are marked "candidate" and excluded from the required plan.
- [ ] Document explicitly enumerates characteristics we will NOT write to, with rationale.
- [ ] Decision covers both trackers (left/red vs right/blue) noting any per-hand differences.
- [ ] Go/no-go recommendation is captured explicitly; M11-03 cannot proceed until this issue is closed with a GO decision.

## Non-goals

- No code changes; recommendation only.
- No offline-sync or session-command decisions (M15).

## Notes

- References §12.1 safety rules, §12.3 adapter contract, §4.2 capability ladder.
- Downstream: M11-03 implements the confirmed plan.

issues.title: Implement buildInitializationPlan in FightCampV1Adapter
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 2 / M11. Translate the confirmed init sequence from M11-02 into `FightCampV1Adapter.buildInitializationPlan(ctx)` returning an ordered `GattOperation[]` per the adapter contract in §12.3. Only writes with triple-evidence may appear; candidates are commented out. Because this is the first task in Phase 2 that writes to real hardware, it is gated by policy review under §12.1.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `src/protocol/fightcamp-v1/FightCampV1Commands.ts` exports the ordered initialization operations with inline comments citing capture IDs.
- [ ] `FightCampV1Adapter.buildInitializationPlan` returns those operations for a valid `InitializationContext`.
- [ ] All writes target characteristics observed in official-app traffic; no speculative writes are emitted (§12.1) — enforced by the M11-04 allowlist.
- [ ] Notification/indication subscriptions are represented as explicit operations, not as side effects.
- [ ] Unit test asserts the exact operation ordering and payloads against a fixture derived from the confirmed capture.
- [ ] On a physical tablet, running the plan against a real tracker produces the same post-init notifications as the official app for the "connect only, no punches" scenario.
- [ ] Policy-review sign-off from M11-02 GO decision is linked in the PR description.

## Non-goals

- No decoding of the notifications produced (M12/M13).
- No session start/stop commands (M15).

## Notes

- Files per §16: `src/protocol/fightcamp-v1/FightCampV1Adapter.ts`, `FightCampV1Commands.ts`.
- Domain code must not import RN/Expo/SQLite/BLE (§15.1) — `GattOperation` is a plain data type.

issues.title: Enforce observed-writes UUID allowlist in GATT dispatcher
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 2 / M11. §12.1 requires that we never write to a GATT characteristic whose meaning has not been observed in official-app traffic. Turn that rule into an executable guardrail: a UUID allowlist derived from M11-01's inventory that the `GattOperationQueue` and `buildInitializationPlan` dispatcher consult before any write is enqueued.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `src/protocol/fightcamp-v1/FightCampV1Commands.ts` (or a sibling) exports `OBSERVED_WRITE_UUIDS`, a constant list derived from `docs/protocol/init-diff.md` with source citations in comments.
- [ ] The GATT dispatcher (per §11.4 `GattOperationQueue`) refuses any `write` / `write-without-response` operation whose characteristic UUID is not in the allowlist and raises a typed error that is logged with the offending UUID.
- [ ] Notification/indication subscriptions (CCCD writes) are permitted independently of the punch-write allowlist but still logged.
- [ ] Unit test verifies: (a) an allowlisted write passes, (b) a non-allowlisted write is refused and never reaches the transport, (c) a CCCD subscription is not blocked.
- [ ] Adding a UUID to the allowlist requires citing a capture ID; a lint or code-review checklist item enforces this.

## Non-goals

- Defining the initialization payloads themselves (M11-03).
- Session commands or offline-sync writes (M15) — those must also pass through this allowlist.

## Notes

- References §12.1 safety rules and §11.4 component boundaries.
- The allowlist is the single chokepoint for §12.1 compliance across M11, M15-01, and M15-02.

issues.title: Scaffold FightCampV1Adapter and register it with ProtocolRegistry
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 2 / M12. Create the adapter skeleton implementing `TrackerProtocolAdapter` (§12.3) with stub methods that throw "not implemented" and register it with `ProtocolRegistry`. Establishes the surface later milestones fill in.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `src/protocol/fightcamp-v1/FightCampV1Adapter.ts` exports a class implementing every method in the §12.3 contract: `scoreAdvertisement`, `inspectGatt`, `buildInitializationPlan`, `decodeFrame`, and optional `buildStartSession`, `buildStopSession`, `buildOfflineSync`, `buildSleepCommand`.
- [ ] `id` and `version` fields are set (id `fightcamp-v1`, version follows semver).
- [ ] Adapter is registered in `src/protocol/ProtocolRegistry.ts`.
- [ ] Adapter and its dependencies do not import RN, Expo, SQLite, or BLE modules (§15.1).
- [ ] Unit test verifies registry lookup by id returns this adapter instance.

## Non-goals

- Do not implement any method beyond stubs (later issues own those).

## Notes

- Files per §16 under `src/protocol/fightcamp-v1/`.
- Reference §11.4 component boundaries.

issues.title: Implement scoreAdvertisement and inspectGatt
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 2 / M12. Implement adapter methods that let the registry match a scanned advertisement and inspect a discovered GATT tree to decide whether this is a FightCamp v1 tracker (§12.3, §4.2 capability ladder).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `scoreAdvertisement(ad)` returns a numeric confidence based on manufacturer data, service UUIDs, or advertised name observed in Phase 1 captures.
- [ ] `inspectGatt(gatt)` returns a `ProtocolInspection` recording which required services/characteristics are present, missing, or unexpected.
- [ ] Both methods are pure and covered by fixture-driven unit tests using Phase 1 advertisement and GATT snapshots.
- [ ] Confidence scoring is documented in code comments citing capture IDs.
- [ ] No writes are attempted from either method (§12.1).

## Non-goals

- Frame decoding (M12-03/M13).
- Capability confidence for velocity/punch-type fields (M14-03).

## Notes

- Files: `src/protocol/fightcamp-v1/FightCampV1Adapter.ts`.
- Fixtures under `src/protocol/fightcamp-v1/fixtures/` per §16.

issues.title: Implement decodeFrame skeleton with DecodeResult union
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 2 / M12. Introduce `FightCampV1Decoder` with a `decodeFrame(frame, state)` entry point returning the DecodeResult union from §12.3 (one punch event, multiple recovered events, device status, ack, clock/sync, unknown, malformed). Wire it through the adapter. Later milestones fill in specific decoders.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `src/protocol/fightcamp-v1/FightCampV1Decoder.ts` exports `decodeFrame` used by the adapter.
- [ ] All seven `DecodeResult` variants from §12.3 are represented in the union type and each is reachable from at least one code branch (or an explicit TODO with fixture reference).
- [ ] Unknown frames return the `unknown` variant with the raw bytes preserved; malformed/truncated frames return `malformed` and never throw (§21.2).
- [ ] Decoder receives and returns a `ProtocolState` value; state mutation is expressed as a returned next-state, not in-place.
- [ ] `decoderId` and `decoderVersion` are stamped on all emitted events (see M12-07 for the version-bump contract).

## Non-goals

- Actual field decoding beyond status framing (M12-04 onward).

## Notes

- Domain-pure module (§15.1). RawBleFrame contract per §12.4.

issues.title: Decode device status and battery frames
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 2 / M12 task 4. From replay fixtures, identify frames that report device status (battery, connection health, sleep) and decode them into structured status messages surfaced by `decodeFrame` (§12.3, §4.2 capability ladder — battery state row).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Decoder recognizes at least the battery-level status frame with byte offsets and scaling documented in `docs/protocol/status-frames.md`.
- [ ] Emitted `deviceStatus` result includes `batteryPercent` when confidently decoded, and `null` otherwise (no guessed value).
- [ ] Unknown status subtypes emit a `deviceStatus` with `subtype: 'unknown'` and preserve the raw payload; they never crash.
- [ ] Fixture unit tests cover left and right trackers, with at least one "low battery" capture if available.
- [ ] Capability flag `hasBatteryState` is set on the protocol inspection when the frame is observed.

## Non-goals

- Punch-event decoding (M13).
- Battery UI treatment (deferred).

## Notes

- Never label unknown bytes as a specific meaning without triple-evidence (§12.1).

issues.title: Unit tests: endianness, fixed-point, and frame-length validation
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 2 / M12. Establish the pure-domain unit-test suite required by §21.1 for the decoder helpers: endianness conversion, fixed-point scaling, and frame-length validation. These tests run without BLE hardware or fixtures and guard the decoder primitives used across M12–M15.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Tests cover little-endian and big-endian readers for u8/u16/u32/i16/i32 including sign-extension edge cases.
- [ ] Fixed-point decoder tests cover Q-format scaling used by candidate velocity fields and assert round-trip stability for known inputs.
- [ ] Frame-length validator tests cover: exact expected length, short frame (truncated), long frame (extra bytes), and empty frame — none of which may throw; all return `malformed` or an explicit validation error.
- [ ] Tests live under `src/protocol/fightcamp-v1/__tests__/` and run in CI without any native or BLE dependencies.
- [ ] Coverage of the decoder helper module is at least 90%.

## Non-goals

- Fixture-based replay tests (M16-03).

## Notes

- Referenced by §21.1 unit-test list. Keep helpers pure per §15.1.

issues.title: Stamp RawBleFrame.monotonicTimeMs from a monotonic clock at ingest
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 2 / M12. `RawBleFrame` (§12.4) carries both `monotonicTimeMs` and `wallTimeIso`. §18.3 requires monotonic time for ordering, latency, and cue windows; wall time is display-only. Capture ingestion must therefore stamp `monotonicTimeMs` from a clock source that is not perturbed by system-clock jumps (NTP resync, manual set, timezone change).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `src/capture/BleCaptureService.ts` (per §16) obtains `monotonicTimeMs` from a monotonic source (RN `performance.now()` origin-locked at app start, or a native `SystemClock.elapsedRealtime()` bridge) and never from `Date.now()`.
- [ ] `wallTimeIso` is stamped from wall time at the same call site and is marked in code comments as informational only.
- [ ] A unit test simulates a wall-clock jump (forwards and backwards) between two frames and asserts that `monotonicTimeMs` remains monotonically increasing and that ordering by `monotonicTimeMs` matches ingest order.
- [ ] A second unit test asserts that `wallTimeIso` reflects the simulated jump (proving the two clocks are independent).
- [ ] Documentation snippet in `docs/protocol/frame-clock.md` records the chosen clock source and its guarantees.

## Non-goals

- Cross-device clock synchronization.
- Tracker-side timestamp decoding (M13-03).

## Notes

- References §12.4 raw-frame contract and §18.3 time-source rules.
- Domain code must not import RN/Expo (§15.1) — the clock accessor lives at the infrastructure boundary and is injected into domain via a plain function.

issues.title: decoderId and decoderVersion stamping with bump discipline
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 2 / M12. `TrackerPunchEvent` (§12.5) requires `decoderId` and `decoderVersion` on every emitted event so stored sessions can be recalculated after a decoder change (§3.2 engineering goal) and replay fixtures can pin expected output to a specific decoder version. This task establishes the contract: where the version lives, when it must bump, and how tests enforce that bumps happen.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `FightCampV1Adapter.version` is the single source of truth for `decoderVersion` and follows semver; `decoderId` is the constant `'fightcamp-v1'`.
- [ ] Every code path in `FightCampV1Decoder` that emits a `punchEvent`, `deviceStatus`, or recovered event stamps both fields from the adapter, verified by a unit test that walks every DecodeResult variant.
- [ ] `docs/protocol/decoder-version.md` documents the bump rules: patch for internal refactors that preserve output, minor for new decoded fields, major for any change that alters existing event bytes-to-fields mapping.
- [ ] Replay fixtures (M16-02) include a `decoderVersion` field in their `expected` block; ReplayRunner (M16-01) fails when the current adapter version differs from the fixture's pinned version unless the fixture is regenerated.
- [ ] A CI check (or a `pnpm test:decoder-version` script) fails when decoder source under `src/protocol/fightcamp-v1/` changes without a version bump, unless the PR includes a `decoder-noop` label or file comment.

## Non-goals

- Migrating historical events across decoder versions (§8.6 handles recompute).

## Notes

- References §12.5 event contract and §3.2 engineering goals.
- Consumed by M13-04, M16-02, M16-03.

issues.title: Identify punch-event frame boundaries
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 2 / M13 task 5. Using controlled captures (single left, single right, five-punch bursts), determine which characteristic and byte pattern delimits a punch event, so `decodeFrame` can emit exactly one `TrackerPunchEvent` per physical punch (§12.3, §12.5).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Document `docs/protocol/punch-frames.md` names the characteristic UUID(s) carrying punch events with evidence from at least three independent captures per scenario.
- [ ] Decoder correctly emits one `punchEvent` result per punch for the "exactly five left punches with two-second gaps" fixture.
- [ ] Boundary detection tolerates concatenated frames and split notifications (if observed) without producing duplicates or losses.
- [ ] Ambiguous frames are classified `unknown`, not `punchEvent`, until evidence permits.
- [ ] `sourceFrameId` on every emitted event points back to a persisted `RawBleFrame` (§12.4).

## Non-goals

- Field-level decoding of hand/sequence/velocity (M13-02..04, M14).

## Notes

- Raw frames must already be persisted before decoding (§12.4).

issues.title: Assign hand identity to decoded punch events
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 2 / M13 task 6. Determine hand attribution — whether hand is inferred from source device (per Hykso, blue=left/red=right, §4.1) or carried in the frame payload — and populate `hand` on `TrackerPunchEvent` (§12.5, §4.2 capability ladder).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Decoder sets `hand` to `'left'` or `'right'` for controlled per-hand captures, and to `'unknown'` when evidence is insufficient.
- [ ] Hand-source strategy (device-derived vs frame-derived) is documented with evidence.
- [ ] Capability inspection flags whether the frame itself encodes hand identity (for §4.2 "left/right device identity" row).
- [ ] Unit fixtures exist for: left-only, right-only, and alternating-punches captures — hand assignments match ground truth.
- [ ] `handAtCapture` on the `RawBleFrame` is honored as fallback when frame-level hand is absent.

## Non-goals

- Velocity/type decoding (M14).

## Notes

- Never overwrite a confidently decoded hand with the device-derived guess.

issues.title: Decode tracker sequence / event ID and timestamp fields
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 2 / M13 task 7. Identify whether the tracker emits a monotonically increasing sequence number and/or a tracker-local timestamp per punch, and populate `sequence` and `trackerTimestampMs` on `TrackerPunchEvent` (§12.5). Supports the sequence-based dedup path in §12.6.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Decoder populates `sequence` when a sequence field is confirmed with triple-evidence; otherwise the field is left undefined.
- [ ] Decoder populates `trackerTimestampMs` when a tracker timestamp is confirmed; otherwise undefined.
- [ ] Wraparound behavior for the sequence field (bit width, reset semantics) is documented in `docs/protocol/sequence.md`.
- [ ] Capability flags `hasSequenceNumber` and `hasTrackerTimestamp` are set in inspection output.
- [ ] Fixture tests cover: single-punch, five-punch burst (verify monotonic sequence), and disconnect/reconnect (verify wraparound-vs-reset heuristic).

## Non-goals

- Dedup implementation (M15-03/04).

## Notes

- If no sequence exists, this issue documents that fact and closes; downstream falls back to compound-key dedup (§12.6).

issues.title: Emit deterministic TrackerPunchEvent for controlled left and right punches
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 2 / M13 vertical slice.
