issues.title: Sequence-based deduplication and gap detection
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 2 / M15. When a tracker sequence field is confirmed (M13-03), implement the preferred dedup path from §12.6: use sequence to drop duplicates, detect forward gaps, distinguish wraparound from reset, persist the last acknowledged/synchronized sequence per tracker, and preserve out-of-order arrival while sorting event time deterministically.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Dedup component maintains per-device `(connectionGeneration, lastSequence)` state and persists the last acknowledged/synchronized sequence per tracker so it survives process restart (§12.6).
- [ ] Duplicate sequence values mark the second event's `qualityFlags` with `likely-duplicate` and exclude it from default metrics — the raw frame is never deleted (§12.6) and remains queryable.
- [ ] Forward gaps produce a `qualityFlags: ['sequence-gap']` marker on the first post-gap event and are logged.
- [ ] Wraparound is distinguished from device reset using `connectionGeneration` and a documented threshold; unit tests cover both cases.
- [ ] Out-of-order arrivals are preserved (never dropped) and sorted by a deterministic event-time key (tracker timestamp when present, else receive monotonic time) so replayed input yields identical order.
- [ ] Recovered events from offline sync are reconciled against real-time events without double-counting.
- [ ] Fixture tests cover: normal sequence, duplicate, gap, wraparound, reset, out-of-order arrival, and offline recovery overlap.

## Non-goals

- Fallback compound-key dedup (M15-04).

## Notes

- Domain-pure module under `src/domain/punch/` per §15.1 / §16.

- [ ] Repository exposes idempotent insert semantics so replays never create duplicate rows.
- [ ] Fixture test replays the same capture twice and asserts identical event and raw-frame counts after the second run.
- [ ] Never deletes raw frames as part of dedup (§12.6) — verified by a test that counts `raw_ble_frames` rows before and after dedup and asserts equality.

epic.title: [EPIC] Phase 3 — Velocity Lab calibration
epic.body:
## Objectives

- Create repeatable per-hand calibration profiles for each tracker.
- Distinguish clearly between raw, calibrated, and normalized (indexed) tracker-reported velocity values throughout the pipeline.
- Give the athlete a guided procedure (idle / low / normal / fast) with sample review, robust percentiles, versioned storage, and a 30-second live validation round.
- Provide a left-vs-right distribution comparison view so the athlete can confirm hand parity before running real sessions.

## Milestones

- M17 — Calibration session, guided punch sets, and L/R distribution comparison
- M18 — Versioned calibration profiles, stale detection, and Layer 4 hooks
- M19 — Live validation round and calibration report

## Definition of done

The user can calibrate left and right separately, repeat the procedure, compare their distributions side by side in Velocity Lab, and test an active profile in a live 30-second run.

Additionally:

- Every persisted event retains both `velocityRaw` and `velocityCalibrated` (§10.3).
- Percentile math guards against zero-width ranges, missing samples, decoder changes, and stale profiles.
- Normalized `velocityIndex = 100 * clamp((velocityCalibrated - p10) / (p90 - p10), 0, 1.25)` is implemented with a zero-width guard (§10.3).
- Default relative zones (Z1 ≤ P35, Z2 ≤ P70, Z3 ≤ P90, Z4 > P90) are derived, persisted, and surfaced to consumers (§10.1 Layer 3).
- Stale-profile triggers from §10.4 are enforced (decoder version, different physical tracker for a hand, firmware change, placement change, external-reference method change, user reset).
- Layer 4 data-model hooks (`externalReferenceMethod`, `estimatedError`, `sourceUnit`, `displayUnit`) exist on the profile and the display gate refuses absolute physical-unit rendering unless a saved external validation record exists (§10.1 Layer 4, §4.3).

## Non-goals

- Layer 4 external absolute calibration itself (high-frame-rate video mapping) is out of scope for this phase; only the data-model hooks and the display gate exist.
- punchCraft and Puncheokie session flows (phases 4 and 5) are not built here.
- Cloud sync or multi-user profile sharing.
- Changing the protocol adapter or decoder — Phase 3 consumes what Phase 2 produces.

## Sub-issues

GitHub auto-populates this list from linked issues in this milestone group; do not maintain it manually.

issues.title: Implement CalibrationEngine state machine for guided per-hand session
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 3 / M17 introduces the calibration session. Per §10.1 Layer 3, a per-hand calibration follows a fixed sequence: confirm placement -> 10 s idle -> 10 low -> 10 normal -> 10 fast -> optional hook/uppercut -> sample review -> percentile calculation -> save versioned profile -> 30 s live validation. This task delivers the pure-domain state machine at `src/domain/calibration/CalibrationEngine.ts` that drives that sequence, independent of UI, BLE, and storage (§15.1, §11.4).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `CalibrationEngine` exposes states: `idle-baseline`, `set-low`, `set-normal`, `set-fast`, `optional-types`, `review`, `percentiles`, `saved`, `validation`, `complete`, `aborted`.
- [ ] Engine accepts normalized `PunchEvent` inputs (from Phase 2) and rejects events for the wrong hand.
- [ ] Each active set requires the configured sample count (default 10) before advancing; idle-baseline uses a 10 s wall-clock window.
- [ ] Engine emits transitions synchronously and never imports React Native, Expo, SQLite, or BLE modules (§15.1).
- [ ] Unit tests cover normal flow, abort at each state, mid-set device disconnect, and wrong-hand event rejection (§21.1).
- [ ] Engine is deterministic given the same event stream and seed.

## Non-goals

- UI screens (M17-02).
- Percentile computation (M17-04).
- Persistence (M18-01).

## Notes

File: `src/domain/calibration/CalibrationEngine.ts`; types alongside `CalibrationProfile.ts`. See §10.1 Layer 3 for the canonical sequence and §22 Phase 3 task 1.

issues.title: Build guided low/normal/fast calibration punch-set UI in Velocity Lab
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 3 / M17. §7.2.D describes the Velocity Lab Calibration workspace. This story is the vertical slice a user experiences: pick a hand, follow the guided prompts through idle -> low -> normal -> fast, see live counters and rolling raw values, and reach the review step. UI binds to `CalibrationEngine` (M17-01) and consumes normalized events from Phase 2.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Route under `src/app/velocity-lab/calibration/` walks the athlete through placement confirmation, then each set with a large counter and current-set label.
- [ ] Idle-baseline set shows a 10 s countdown and lists any spurious events captured during it.
- [ ] Each punch set shows accepted count (default target 10), rejected count, and the most recent raw value (labelled `tracker-reported velocity`, never `force` / `power` / `impact speed` / `energy` per §4.3).
- [ ] User can pause, resume, and abort at any state; abort discards unsaved samples.
- [ ] Wrong-hand event visibly counted as rejected with reason.
- [ ] Reaches the review screen (M17-03) with all set samples in memory.

## Non-goals

- Percentile math and profile persistence.
- External-reference (Layer 4) capture.

## Notes

Components live under `src/app/velocity-lab/calibration/` and reuse `src/components/MetricTile.tsx`. Binds to `state/useDeviceStore.ts` for the selected tracker + hand. See §7.2.D, §7.3, §10.1 Layer 3, §22 Phase 3 task 2. Hardware helpful for manual verification but not blocking for review.

issues.title: Add sample review and rejection UI for calibration sets
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 3 / M17. §10.1 Layer 3 step 7 requires the athlete to review rejected samples and obvious false positives before percentiles are computed. This story adds the review screen and the rejection toggle on individual samples inside a completed calibration session, exercised on real hardware captures.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Review screen lists samples grouped by set (idle / low / normal / fast, plus optional types) with raw value, timestamp offset from set start, hand, and current include/exclude state.
- [ ] Athlete can toggle inclusion of any sample; excluded samples are visually distinct and excluded from percentile inputs.
- [ ] Auto-flagged samples (below `lowerValid` or above `upperValid`, cross-hand, duplicate) are pre-marked as excluded with a reason chip.
- [ ] Undo/redo of exclusions within the review session.
- [ ] `CalibrationEngine` state advances to `percentiles` only after the user confirms the review.
- [ ] Raw sample values remain immutable throughout review (§12.1); only include/exclude flags are toggled.

## Non-goals

- Editing raw values (raw is immutable per §12.1).
- Re-shooting a single set (out of scope; user aborts and restarts).

## Notes

See §22 Phase 3 task 3. Included/excluded flag is engine-local until profile save; raw samples are never mutated. Requires real tracker captures for meaningful exercise.

issues.title: Compute robust percentiles (P10/P35/P50/P70/P90) with zero-width guard
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 3 / M17. §10.1 Layer 3 step 8 and §10.3 require robust percentile calculation on accepted samples per hand, producing P10, P35, P50, P70, P90 for zone assignment (§10.1) and normalized-index math. §10.3 explicitly requires guarding against zero-width percentile ranges, missing samples, decoder changes, and stale profiles. §21.1 lists percentile calculations as a unit-test target.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Pure function in `src/domain/calibration/CalibrationEngine.ts` (or sibling module) computes P10/P35/P50/P70/P90 from the accepted-sample array using a documented interpolation method (e.g. type-7 linear).
- [ ] Function returns a typed result including `sampleCount` and a `degenerate` flag when fewer than a configurable minimum accepted samples exist (default 15 across low/normal/fast combined) or when `p90 - p10 == 0`.
- [ ] Downstream index calculation `100 * clamp((v - p10) / (p90 - p10), 0, 1.25)` short-circuits to `undefined` when the range is zero-width and never divides by zero (§10.3).
- [ ] Unit tests per §21.1 cover: monotonic distribution, all-equal samples (zero-width), single sample, fewer than minimum samples, deterministic output given identical inputs, and mixed-hand rejection upstream.
- [ ] Function is deterministic and has no RN/Expo/SQLite/BLE imports (§15.1).

## Non-goals

- Zone display in punchCraft UI (Phase 4).
- External-reference (Layer 4) model fitting.

## Notes

See §10.1 (default zone boundaries), §10.3 (transformation and guards), §21.1 (percentile unit tests), §22 Phase 3 task 4.

issues.title: Left-vs-right calibration distribution comparison view
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 3 / M17 and the epic DoD (`compare distributions`) require a Velocity Lab surface that overlays the currently active (or in-review) left and right calibration distributions side by side so the athlete can catch obvious hand asymmetry — wildly different sample counts, badly separated P10/P90 bands, or clearly bimodal sets — before either profile becomes active. §7.2.D lists 'comparing left and right profiles' as a first-class calibration workspace responsibility.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Route under `src/app/velocity-lab/calibration/compare/` renders the left and right calibration distributions as overlaid histograms (or a paired violin/box) with P10/P35/P50/P70/P90 lines from the active profile for each hand.
- [ ] Numeric side-by-side table shows per-hand `sampleCount`, P10/P35/P50/P70/P90, `decoderVersion`, `active`, and `stale_reason` (if any) from `CalibrationRepository` (§10.2, §10.4).
- [ ] View works when only one hand has a profile (renders the missing hand as an empty-state chip, not a crash), and when either profile is degenerate/zero-width (renders `index unavailable` copy, not NaN).
- [ ] All velocity axes and tiles are labelled `tracker-reported velocity` (§4.3); absolute physical units are never shown unless the profile carries a Layer 4 validation record (see M18-05 display gate).
- [ ] Stale profiles render with a visible stale badge and their percentile lines are drawn muted so the user does not confuse a stale distribution for the active one (§10.4).
- [ ] Deep-link from the review screen (M17-03) after both hands have been calibrated at least once in the current session.

## Non-goals

- Editing profiles from this view (recalibration is a separate flow).
- Exporting the comparison (covered by the report in M19-02).

## Notes

Binds to `CalibrationRepository` via a projection in `state/useDeviceStore.ts`; charts live in `src/components/` (new `DistributionChart.tsx`). See §7.2.D, §10.1 Layer 3, §22 Phase 3. Hardware required to produce two hand distributions worth comparing.

issues.title: Add calibration_profiles schema and CalibrationRepository
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 3 / M18. §17.1 declares the `calibration_profiles` table (fields from §10.2 plus activation and invalidation metadata). This task adds the migration and the `src/storage/repositories/CalibrationRepository.ts` that persists, reads, versions, activates, and marks-stale profiles. Domain-layer `CalibrationProfile` in `src/domain/calibration/CalibrationProfile.ts` stays pure (§15.1); only the repository touches SQLite.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Migration adds `calibration_profiles` with every §10.2 field: `id`, `version`, `deviceId`, `hand`, `decoderVersion`, `method`, `sourceUnit`, `displayUnit`, `scale`, `offset`, `lowerValid`, `upperValid`, `p10`, `p35`, `p50`, `p70`, `p90`, `externalReferenceMethod`, `estimatedError`, `sampleCount`, `createdAt`, `active`.
- [ ] Migration also adds invalidation metadata columns: `stale_reason`, `stale_at`, `invalidated_by_profile_id`.
- [ ] Migration adds baseline snapshot columns required by the M18-03 CalibrationInvalidator (§10.4 triggers): `firmware_revision_at_calibration`, `placement_note_hash_at_calibration`, `external_reference_method_at_calibration`. These are frozen at `insertProfile` time so a later edit to `tracker_devices` cannot mask a stale trigger.
- [ ] Migration adds derived-zone columns `zone1_upper`, `zone2_upper`, `zone3_upper` (defaults P35/P70/P90) so consumers can read the effective zone thresholds without re-deriving.
- [ ] Unique constraint (or enforced-in-repo invariant) that at most one `active = true` profile exists per `(deviceId, hand)` at a time.
- [ ] `CalibrationRepository` exposes `insertProfile`, `listByDeviceHand`, `getActive(deviceId, hand)`, `activate(profileId)` (auto-deactivates prior), `markStale(profileId, reason)`, `getById(profileId)` (returns stale profiles too, for historical reprocessing per §10.4). `insertProfile` snapshots the current `tracker_devices.firmware_revision`, hashes the current placement note, and freezes the external-reference method into the three baseline columns above so M18-03 has a stable diff target.
- [ ] `version` monotonically increments per `(deviceId, hand)`; repo assigns it.
- [ ] Retention: calibration profiles and their referenced captures are kept indefinitely while referenced by any session (§17.2); repo never deletes a profile still cited by `sessions.left_calibration_id` / `right_calibration_id`.
- [ ] Repo unit tests use an in-memory SQLite fixture and cover activation swap, stale marking, retention refusal-to-delete-when-referenced, and version monotonicity.
- [ ] No domain code imports the repository directly (only via injected interfaces).

## Non-goals

- Stale-detection trigger wiring (M18-03).
- UI surfacing of profile history (M19-02 report will show recent).

## Notes

Files: `src/storage/migrations/*_calibration_profiles.ts`, `src/storage/repositories/CalibrationRepository.ts`, `src/domain/calibration/CalibrationProfile.ts`. See §10.2, §10.4, §17.1, §17.2, §22 Phase 3 task 5.

issues.title: Create and activate versioned calibration profiles with derived zone thresholds
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 3 / M18. §22 Phase 3 task 5 requires creating and activating profile versions from the output of a completed calibration session. This wires `CalibrationEngine`'s `saved` transition to `CalibrationRepository.insertProfile` + `activate`, capturing decoder version, sample count, computed percentiles, identity fingerprint of the physical tracker (§10.2, §11.7), and the derived §10.1 Layer 3 zone thresholds (Z1 ≤ P35, Z2 ≤ P70, Z3 ≤ P90, Z4 > P90).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] On `saved`, the engine emits a `CalibrationProfile` DTO with `method: 'relative-zones'`, `sourceUnit: 'unknown'` (unless Layer 4 is present), `displayUnit: 'index'`, `scale=1`, `offset=0`, filled percentiles, `sampleCount`, `decoderVersion`, `deviceId`, `hand`, `createdAt`, `active: true`.
- [ ] Zone thresholds `zone1_upper=p35`, `zone2_upper=p70`, `zone3_upper=p90` are derived and persisted on the profile so downstream consumers (punchCraft, Puncheokie, validation UI) read a single source of truth (§10.1 Layer 3).
- [ ] Zone thresholds are configurable: a `zoneOverrides` input (per-hand percentile keys) can override the defaults without changing the raw percentiles.
- [ ] A save handler persists via `CalibrationRepository`, activates the new version, and returns the assigned `id` and `version`.
- [ ] Previously active profile for the same `(deviceId, hand)` is deactivated but retained (per §10.4 stale profiles remain for historical reprocessing).
- [ ] Failure to persist rolls back activation state in the store and surfaces an error toast in the Velocity Lab.
- [ ] Integration test with in-memory SQLite verifies the activation swap and zone-threshold persistence.

## Non-goals

- Applying the profile to live events (M18-04).
- Report export (M19-02).

## Notes

See §10.1 Layer 3 (default zones), §10.2, §10.4, §22 Phase 3 task 5.

issues.title: Detect and enforce stale calibration profiles per §10.4 triggers
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 3 / M18. §10.4 lists six invalidation triggers: decoder-version bump (incompatible), different physical tracker assigned to a hand, tracker firmware change, material placement change, external-reference method change, and explicit user reset. Stale profiles must remain readable for historical session reprocessing but must not be applied silently to new sessions (§10.4).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A `CalibrationInvalidator` in `src/domain/calibration/` inspects an active profile against current device state and returns a typed `StaleReason` or `null`. Inputs include the profile's stored `decoderVersion`, the device's `identity_fingerprint` and `firmware_revision` from `tracker_devices` (§17.1), the current placement-note hash, and the external-reference method key.
- [ ] Detects the 'different physical tracker for hand' trigger by comparing the profile's `deviceId` and the current `identity_fingerprint` on `tracker_devices`, not by display name alone (§11.7).
- [ ] Detects the firmware trigger by comparing the profile's captured `firmwareRevisionAtCalibration` against `tracker_devices.firmware_revision`.
- [ ] On Velocity Lab load and before any session-start read of `getActive`, the invalidator runs; stale profiles are marked via `CalibrationRepository.markStale` with the reason and are NOT returned by `getActive` for live application.
- [ ] User-initiated reset marks the current active profile stale with reason `user-reset`.
- [ ] UI in Velocity Lab shows a stale badge with the reason and offers `recalibrate`.
- [ ] Unit tests cover each of the six triggers plus a no-change case.
- [ ] Historical session reprocessing paths (Phase 4+) can still read stale profiles by `id`.

## Non-goals

- Automatic re-run of calibration.
- Firmware detection mechanism itself (consumes what §11 already surfaces).

## Notes

See §10.4, §11.7, §17.1, §22 Phase 3 task 7. Placement note lives on `tracker_devices` per §17.1.

issues.title: Apply active calibration to events preserving raw, calibrated, and normalized index
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 3 / M18. §10.3 mandates that every event retain both `velocityRaw` and `velocityCalibrated`, computes a normalized personal index `velocityIndex = 100 * clamp((velocityCalibrated - p10) / (p90 - p10), 0, 1.25)`, and requires guards against zero-width ranges, missing samples, decoder changes, and stale profiles. §12.1 forbids mutating raw evidence. This task adds a pure calibration transform used by the live pipeline and by historical reprocessing.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `applyCalibration(event, profile)` in `src/domain/calibration/CalibrationEngine.ts` (or sibling) returns a new event object with `velocityRaw` unchanged and `velocityCalibrated = max(0, velocityRaw * scale + offset)`.
- [ ] `velocityIndex` is computed only when the profile carries usable P10/P90 and `p90 - p10 > 0`; otherwise it is `undefined` and a `qualityFlag` of `index-unavailable` is set. Never emits NaN or Infinity (§10.3 zero-width guard, per M17-04).
- [ ] When `profile` is `null`, `velocityCalibrated` is `undefined` and `qualityFlag` `no-active-profile` is set; `velocityRaw` still populated (§10.3, §12.1).
- [ ] When `profile` is stale, `applyCalibration` refuses to produce `velocityCalibrated` or `velocityIndex` and sets `qualityFlag` `stale-profile`; `velocityRaw` is always still populated so the raw evidence is not lost (§10.4, §12.1).
- [ ] When the event's `decoderVersion` does not equal the profile's `decoderVersion`, the transform refuses to produce `velocityCalibrated` and sets `qualityFlag` `decoder-version-mismatch`; `velocityRaw` still populated.
- [ ] When the profile is missing any of P10/P35/P50/P70/P90 (`degenerate` from M17-04 or missing samples), `velocityCalibrated` may still be produced but `velocityIndex` is `undefined` with `qualityFlag` `missing-percentiles`.
- [ ] `PunchEventRepository` writes preserve raw, calibrated, and index columns plus the active profile id used.
- [ ] Unit tests per §21.1 cover: happy path, stale profile refusal, decoder-version-mismatch refusal, null profile, zero-width percentile range, missing-percentiles fallback, and negative computed value clamped to 0. Tests assert `velocityRaw` is preserved in every failure branch.
- [ ] Function has no RN/Expo/SQLite/BLE imports (§15.1).

## Non-goals

- Live UI display (Phase 4 punchCraft).
- External-reference absolute-unit display (see M18-05 gate).

## Notes

See §10.3, §10.4, §12.1, §12.4 (raw frames persisted before parsing), §21.1, §22 Phase 3 task 6.

issues.title: Wire Layer 4 external-reference hooks and absolute-unit display gate
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 3 / M18. §10.1 Layer 4 and §4.3 together require that the app never label a value as an absolute physical unit (cm/s, m/s, mph, force, power, energy) unless a saved external validation record backs the active profile. Layer 4 fitting itself is out of scope for this phase, but the data-model hooks and the display gate must exist so consumers can never accidentally render 'impact speed' or 'force' from a relative-zone profile.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `CalibrationProfile` (both TypeScript type in `src/domain/calibration/CalibrationProfile.ts` and the schema column set added in M18-01) carries `externalReferenceMethod?`, `estimatedError?`, `sourceUnit`, and `displayUnit` per §10.2.
- [ ] A pure predicate `hasValidatedAbsoluteUnit(profile): boolean` returns true only when `method === 'external-reference'`, `sourceUnit` is one of `cm/s` / `m/s` / `mph`, `externalReferenceMethod` is a non-empty string, `estimatedError` is a finite non-negative number, and the profile is not stale.
- [ ] A `formatVelocityLabel(profile)` helper returns `'tracker-reported velocity'` for any profile that fails `hasValidatedAbsoluteUnit`, and the profile's `displayUnit` label otherwise (§4.3). The helper never returns `impact speed`, `force`, `power`, or `energy`.
- [ ] All Phase-3 UI (`M17-02`, `M17-03`, `M17-05`, `M19-01`) and the report (`M19-02`) consume `formatVelocityLabel` for their velocity axes and metric-tile labels; a lint or unit test asserts the forbidden strings never appear in Phase-3 view code.
- [ ] Migration (from M18-01) leaves `externalReferenceMethod` and `estimatedError` nullable and defaults `sourceUnit='unknown'`, `displayUnit='index'` for profiles created by M18-02.
- [ ] Unit tests cover: relative-zone profile refused, external-reference profile with missing `estimatedError` refused, valid external-reference profile accepted, stale external-reference profile refused.

## Non-goals

- Building the Layer 4 capture / fitting UI (out of scope for Phase 3).
- Any absolute-unit conversion math beyond `scale`/`offset` already in M18-04.

## Notes

See §4.3, §10.1 Layer 4, §10.2. Files: `src/domain/calibration/CalibrationProfile.ts`, `src/domain/calibration/velocityLabel.ts`.

issues.title: Run 30-second live validation round against the active calibration profile
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 3 / M19. §10.1 Layer 3 step 9 and §22 Phase 3 task 8 require a 30-second live validation round after saving a profile. The athlete throws freely; the app shows raw, calibrated, and normalized-index values in real time, plus zone distribution, so the profile can be sanity-checked before use in a real session.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] From the calibration workspace, athlete can start a 30 s validation round bound to the just-activated profile for the selected hand.
- [ ] Live tiles display current tracker-reported velocity (raw), calibrated value, and normalized index; zone chip (Z1-Z4) updates from the zone thresholds persisted on the profile in M18-02.
- [ ] All velocity labels are produced through `formatVelocityLabel` from M18-05 — never `impact speed`, `force`, `power`, or `energy` (§4.3); absolute physical units render only when the active profile passes `hasValidatedAbsoluteUnit`.
- [ ] Running histogram of accepted samples during the 30 s round, with P10/P35/P70/P90 lines from the active profile overlaid.
- [ ] End of round shows counts per zone and mean/median index; user can `accept` (keep profile active), `recalibrate`, or `mark stale` with reason `user-reset`.
- [ ] Zero-width percentile range or missing percentiles yield explicit `index unavailable` copy, not NaN / Infinity (per M17-04, M18-04).
- [ ] If `CalibrationInvalidator` (M18-03) reports the active profile stale when the round is started, the round is hard-blocked with a modal that names the fired trigger and offers `recalibrate`; it never applies a stale profile silently (§10.4).
- [ ] Both `velocityRaw` and `velocityCalibrated` are written for every accepted event (§10.3); raw is written even on stale-profile / decoder-mismatch refusal paths from M18-04.

## Non-goals

- punchCraft round timer semantics (Phase 4).
- Absolute physical-unit display beyond the M18-05 gate.

## Notes

Route under `src/app/velocity-lab/calibration/validate/`. See §10.1 Layer 3 step 9, §10.3, §10.4, §22 Phase 3 task 8. Physical trackers required for meaningful validation.

issues.title: Export calibration report (versions, percentiles, validation) per hand
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 3 / M19. §22 Phase 3 task 9 requires exporting a calibration report. The report documents each versioned profile per hand with its percentiles, sample counts, decoder version, active/stale status, and the results of any 30-second validation runs. The export is a local artifact (JSON + human-readable Markdown) for the athlete and for support debugging.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `CalibrationReportExporter` in `src/capture/` (alongside `CaptureExporter.ts`) produces a JSON file listing all profiles for `(deviceId, hand)` with full §10.2 fields plus `active`, `stale_reason`, `zone1_upper`/`zone2_upper`/`zone3_upper`, and `validation_summary`.
- [ ] A Markdown rendering summarizes: hand, active version, sample count, P10/P35/P50/P70/P90, derived zone thresholds, decoder version, created-at, stale reason if any, and the most recent validation round's zone counts.
- [ ] Both JSON and Markdown output route every velocity label through `formatVelocityLabel` from M18-05: relative-zone profiles are labelled `tracker-reported velocity` (§4.3); absolute physical units (cm/s, m/s, mph) appear only when the profile passes `hasValidatedAbsoluteUnit` (i.e., a saved external validation record exists per §10.1 Layer 4). The forbidden strings `impact speed`, `force`, `power`, `energy` must never appear in either output.
- [ ] Export writable to device storage via the same share mechanism used by `CaptureExporter`.
- [ ] Unit tests cover: no profiles, only stale profiles, multiple versions, missing validation record, zero-width percentile profile, relative-zone profile (must render `tracker-reported velocity`), and external-reference profile with a saved validation record (may render absolute unit).

## Non-goals

- Cloud upload.
- PDF rendering.

## Notes

See §4.3, §10.1 Layer 4, §16 for file location, §17.1 for source tables, §22 Phase 3 task 9, §21.1 for the associated unit-test surfaces. Kept at P1 because the interactive L/R comparison view (M17-05) is the primary vehicle for the DoD's `compare distributions` requirement; this export is the durable/shareable companion.

epic.title: [EPIC] Phase 4 — punchCraft sessions
epic.body:
## Objectives

- Deliver the first complete training workflow: a timed, multi-round bag session that consumes normalized punch events, presents live glanceable metrics, and can be saved, reopened, and deterministically recalculated.

## Milestones

- M20 — Session/timer engine
- M21 — Readiness gate & live metric tiles
- M22 — Session persistence & deterministic metrics
- M23 — Summary, history, recalculation & export

## Definition of done

- A timed multi-round bag session can be completed, saved, reopened, and deterministically recalculated from stored events (spec §22 Phase 4).
- Pre-session readiness gate blocks/warns on degraded modes (§8.2).
- Pause semantics honor `duringPause` quality flag and exclude paused events from default metrics (§8.4).
- Summary discloses the velocity representation source (§8.5).
- `session_metrics` rows carry `calculation_version` so recalculation with a newer decoder or calibration profile never mutates raw events (§17.1, §8.6).

## Non-goals

- Puncheokie program cues and stance mapping (Phase 5).
- Spotify auth, playlist selection, or playback (Phase 6).
- Any protocol-layer changes or new GATT writes.
- Cloud sync or multi-device history.

## Sub-issues

issues.title: Implement SessionEngine state machine per §18.1
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 4 / M20. Implement the deterministic session state machine defined in §18.1: `configuring → ready → countdown → work ↔ paused, work → rest → work, work/rest → finishing → completed`, plus `cancelled` transitions from `countdown|work|paused`. Lives in `src/domain/session/SessionEngine.ts` and `SessionState.ts` (§16) and must remain free of RN/Expo/SQLite/BLE imports (§15.1).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] State enum and transition table match the §18.1 diagram exactly (including `finishing → completed` gated on metrics-persisted signal).
- [ ] Public API exposes `start`, `pause`, `resume`, `advanceRound`, `skipRest`, `stopAndSave`, `stopAndDiscard`, and emits typed transition events.
- [ ] Unit tests cover every legal transition and reject every illegal transition with a typed error.
- [ ] Engine consumes an injected clock (see M20-05) and never reads wall time directly.
- [ ] No import of `react-native`, `expo-*`, `expo-sqlite`, or any `src/ble/**` module.

## Non-goals

- Persistence (M22) and metric calculation (M22-03).
- UI wiring (M21).

## Notes

- Files: `src/domain/session/SessionEngine.ts`, `SessionState.ts`, `__tests__/SessionEngine.test.ts`.
- Reference §18.1 diagram; keep pure-TS for jest.

issues.title: Add TimerConfig with §8.1 modes and defaults
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 4 / M20. Model the four punchCraft session types — free, single timer, round workout, open rounds — and the initial timer fields/defaults from §8.1 (countdown 10 s, 3 rounds, 3-min work, 1-min rest, final-10-s cue, auto-start off, require both trackers on). Feeds the SessionEngine (M20-01).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `TimerConfig` discriminated union covers all four §8.1 session types: `free` (no timer, manual stop), `single` (single fixed-duration timer), `round` (rounds + rest with configurable count), and `openRounds` (manual round advance, no automatic rest).
- [ ] Defaults match §8.1 exactly for every field and are exposed as a `defaultTimerConfig()` factory (countdown 10 s, 3 rounds, work 180 s, rest 60 s, final-10-s cue on, auto-start off, `requireBothTrackers` on).
- [ ] Validator rejects out-of-range values per §8.1 field ranges (work 15 s–5 min, rest 0 s–5 min, rounds 1–20, countdown 0–60 s (§8.1 verbatim)) with typed errors and field-level error codes.
- [ ] Round-mode config drives correct round count and work/rest sequencing when fed into SessionEngine tests.
- [ ] Open-rounds mode requires manual `advanceRound` and produces no automatic rest transition.
- [ ] Free mode produces no round-boundary events and terminates only on `stopAndSave`/`stopAndDiscard`.
- [ ] Single-timer mode auto-transitions to `finishing` when the timer expires.

## Non-goals

- Persisting `timer_config_json` (M22-01).
- Editor UI (out of scope for Phase 4 beyond field entry on the readiness screen).

## Notes

- File: `src/domain/session/TimerConfig.ts`.
- Reference §8.1 field table verbatim.

issues.title: Implement pause semantics with duringPause quality flag
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 4 / M20. Per §8.4, pausing stops the timer but keeps punch events flowing; those events must be tagged `duringPause` and excluded from default metrics. Touches SessionEngine (M20-01) and `src/domain/punch/PunchQuality.ts`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Adding `duringPause` to the PunchQuality flag set does not break existing quality-flag consumers.
- [ ] While `paused`, timer clock is frozen but incoming normalized events are recorded and stamped with `duringPause`.
- [ ] Default metric queries (M22-03) exclude events carrying `duringPause`.
- [ ] Resume transitions the engine back to `work` and unpaused events are no longer flagged.
- [ ] MetricsEngine accepts an `includePausedEvents: boolean` option so post-session reprocessing (M23-02) can honor §8.4's user-toggle.
- [ ] Unit tests cover: pause during work, punch during pause, resume, reprocess-with-paused toggle producing a distinct metric row.

## Non-goals

- Reprocessing UI toggle wiring lives in M23-02.

## Notes

- Files: `src/domain/session/SessionEngine.ts`, `src/domain/punch/PunchQuality.ts`.
- Cross-ref §8.4 pause semantics list.

issues.title: Support tracker reconnect during an active session
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 4 / M20 (control from §8.4). A tracker may drop and re-establish mid-session without discarding the session. The SessionEngine must accept a reconnect signal from `src/ble/TrackerConnection.ts` (via the state layer), continue accepting events on the new connection generation, and log a connection interruption for the summary.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Session survives `disconnect → reconnect` for either hand and remains in its current state.
- [ ] Events from the new connection generation are accepted; events from a stale generation are rejected with a queryable reason (§18.2).
- [ ] A connection-interruption record is emitted per drop with start/end monotonic timestamps for later summary use (§8.5).
- [ ] Reconnect never rewinds the round clock or duplicates round boundaries.
- [ ] Test uses a fake BLE facade — no real BLE imports in the domain layer.
- [ ] Hardware smoke: verified against paired left and right trackers by toggling each tracker's connection mid-session; interruption records match observed drops.

## Non-goals

- Recovering punches that occurred while disconnected (degraded-mode warning already surfaces this per §8.2).

## Notes

- Files: `src/domain/session/SessionEngine.ts`, `src/state/useSessionStore.ts`.
- §19 reliability targets depend on this behavior — treat as go/no-go for Phase 4 sign-off.

issues.title: Add monotonic time source per §18.3
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 4 / M20. Per §18.3, the session/timer engine must use a monotonic clock for timer progression, event ordering, cue windows, latency, and round boundaries; ISO wall time is only for history display, filenames, and exports. A system-clock change must not move an active round.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `MonotonicClock` interface with `nowMs(): number` and a `TimeSource` bundling monotonic + wall-time providers lives in the domain layer.
- [ ] Default implementation wraps `performance.now()` (or platform equivalent) and is injected into SessionEngine.
- [ ] Test double simulates a wall-clock jump (both forward and backward) during an active work interval and asserts round boundaries and round-clock readings do not move.
- [ ] Test double simulates monotonic time advancing normally while wall time is frozen and confirms round transitions fire at the correct monotonic offsets.
- [ ] All engine timing calls go through the injected clock — grep confirms no `Date.now()` in `src/domain/session/**`.

## Non-goals

- Cross-device time sync.

## Notes

- File: `src/domain/session/TimeSource.ts` (new).

issues.title: Build pre-session readiness gate with degraded-mode warnings
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 4 / M21. Implement the §8.2 readiness screen: left/right tracker readiness, active calibration profile per hand, capability summary, battery when available, Spotify status only when launched from Puncheokie, and an explicit warning when the session will run in a degraded mode from §8.2's examples (right unavailable → left-only, velocity unavailable → count-only, punch-type unavailable → hand/count only, offline recovery unavailable → possible missing punches).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Screen renders all §8.2 fields and hides Spotify status unless entry point is Puncheokie.
- [ ] Start button is disabled until required conditions (per TimerConfig `requireBothTrackers`) are met.
- [ ] Degraded-mode warning: right tracker unavailable surfaces a "left-only session" banner.
- [ ] Degraded-mode warning: tracker-reported velocity unavailable surfaces a "count-only session" banner.
- [ ] Degraded-mode warning: punch-type unavailable surfaces a "hand and count only" banner.
- [ ] Degraded-mode warning: offline recovery unavailable surfaces a "punches may be missed during disconnects" banner.

issues.title: Build live session UI with large glanceable metric tiles and §8.4 controls
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 4 / M21. Implement the default live view per §8.3: round number and timer, total/left/right punch counts, average tracker-reported velocity, current-or-most-recent punch velocity, connection indicators, and pause/stop controls. Also surface the full §8.4 in-session control set. Uses `RoundTimer`, `MetricTile`, and `ConnectionBadge` from §16.

issues.title: Add SQLite schema/migrations for sessions, rounds, punch_events, session_metrics
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 4 / M22. Add SQLite migrations and a read-mostly `SessionRepository` for the §17.1 tables `sessions`, `rounds`, `punch_events`, and `session_metrics`. Persistence lives in `src/storage/**`; the domain layer talks only to the repository interface (§15.1). issues.title: Unit-test event acceptance rules per §18.2

issues.title: Implement MetricsEngine as exclusive writer of session_metrics with calculation_version
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 4 / M22. `MetricsEngine` computes §9.1 confirmed metrics and, when available, §9.2 velocity-dependent metrics, plus §9.5 quality metrics, then writes rows to `session_metrics` including `calculation_version` so recalculation with a newer decoder or newer calibration profile never mutates raw punch_events (§17.1, §8.6). MetricsEngine is the exclusive writer of `session_metrics` — the SessionRepository (M22-01) provides only the schema and read paths. Domain-pure module in `src/domain/metrics/**`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Computes total/left/right counts, left/right %, and per-round counts/rates from accepted events; excludes `duringPause` by default.
- [ ] Computes average/median/max/p90 tracker-reported velocity when velocity is available; omits them otherwise.
- [ ] Computes §9.5 quality metrics: duplicates suppressed, rejected event count with per-reason breakdown, unmatched/malformed counts, and per-tracker gap totals derived from connection-interruption records.
- [ ] Accepts a recalculation input struct: `{ decoderVersion, leftCalibrationId, rightCalibrationId, includePausedEvents }` so both newer-decoder and newer-calibration-profile recalcs (§8.6) reuse the same immutable-raw path.
- [ ] Every persisted row carries `metric_key`, `metric_value`, `metric_unit`, `calculation_version`, `calculated_at`, `decoder_version`, `left_calibration_id`, `right_calibration_id`, and optional `round_id`.
- [ ] `calculation_version` is sourced from a constant exported by `metricDefinitions.ts` and bumped intentionally, not derived from build metadata.
- [ ] Re-running the engine over the same inputs produces the same output bit-for-bit; a bumped `calculation_version` or a changed calibration id writes a new row rather than overwriting.
- [ ] Terminology in metric keys and units avoids force/power/energy (§4.3).

## Non-goals

- Custom-output-index authoring (§9.4).
- Puncheokie cue results (Phase 5).

## Notes

- Files: `src/domain/metrics/MetricsEngine.ts`, `src/domain/metrics/metricDefinitions.ts`.

issues.title: Build session summary with velocity-representation disclosure and §8.5 fields
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 4 / M23. Build the post-session summary per §8.5: durations, counts and percentages, velocity statistics when available, per-round counts/rates and velocity stats, connection interruptions, recovered/malformed counts, active calibration profile/version, user notes, and — mandatory — disclosure of the velocity representation source (confirmed physical unit, tracker unit, calibrated tracker unit, or normalized velocity index).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Summary reads exclusively from `session_metrics` plus the source session/round rows — no recomputation on render.
- [ ] Velocity-representation banner is always rendered when any velocity metric appears and labels the exact §8.5 category (confirmed physical unit / tracker unit / calibrated tracker unit / normalized velocity index).
- [ ] Renders total, left, and right session durations plus active vs paused breakdown.
- [ ] Renders total/left/right punch counts and left/right percentages.
- [ ] Renders session-level average, median, max, and p90 tracker-reported velocity when available.
- [ ] Per-round table shows round number, work duration, counts, rate, and per-round velocity stats (avg/median/max/p90) when available.
- [ ] Renders connection-interruption list with per-drop start/end and total interrupted duration per tracker (even when zero).
- [ ] Renders §9.5 quality metrics: duplicates suppressed, rejected events with per-reason breakdown, unmatched, malformed, and per-tracker gap totals (even when zero).
- [ ] Renders active calibration profile name and version per hand.
- [ ] Notes field is editable and persists back to `sessions.notes`.
- [ ] Terminology uses "tracker-reported velocity" throughout (§4.3).

## Non-goals

- Export (M23-03) and history navigation (M23-02).

## Notes

- Files: `src/app/(punchcraft)/summary/[sessionId].tsx`.
- Reference §8.5 field list verbatim.

issues.title: Build history list, detail, delete-with-captures, and recalc with newer decoder or calibration profile
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 4 / M23. History screen per §8.6: list by date, filter by session type, view details, compare rounds, delete a session with its associated captures, and recalculate metrics with a newer decoder OR a newer calibration profile without altering the original raw event data. Recalculation dispatches MetricsEngine (M22-03) with a bumped `calculation_version` and/or a new calibration id and appends new `session_metrics` rows.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] History list sorted by `started_at` desc with a type filter for `punchcraft` (Velocity Lab and Puncheokie sessions hidden or grouped separately).
- [ ] Detail view links back to the summary (M23-01) for the selected session and lets the user pick which metric version (by `calculation_version` + calibration ids) to display.
- [ ] Recalculate action offers two axes: a decoder-version selector (defaulting to the latest available `metricDefinitions.calculationVersion`) and a per-hand calibration-profile selector (§10).
- [ ] Recalculate re-runs MetricsEngine over stored `punch_events`, writes new `session_metrics` rows with the chosen decoder/calibration ids, and never issues UPDATE/DELETE against `punch_events` — verified by a test that snapshots `punch_events` before and after.
- [ ] Recalculate exposes an "include paused events" toggle that flows through as MetricsEngine's `includePausedEvents` option (§8.4), producing a distinct metric row from the default.
- [ ] Delete-session action removes the session and its associated captures — the `sessions` row, its `rounds`, its `punch_events`, its `session_metrics`, and the associated raw `ble_frames` capture rows scoped to that session's time window — after a two-step confirmation that names what will be deleted.
- [ ] Delete never removes `ble_frames` outside the deleted session's time window and never touches other sessions.

## Non-goals

- Cross-session comparison charts (defer).

## Notes

- Files: `src/app/(punchcraft)/history/index.tsx`, `src/app/(punchcraft)/history/[sessionId].tsx`.
- Reference §8.6.

issues.title: Implement CSV and JSON session export
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 4 / M23 (Phase 4 task 11 and §8.6). Export a completed session as CSV and JSON to a share sheet / local file. Filenames use ISO wall time per §18.3. Exports must include `calculation_version`, decoder version, calibration profile ids/versions, and the velocity-representation label from §8.5 so downstream analysis is unambiguous.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] CSV export writes one row per punch_event with columns: monotonic_time_ms, wall_time_iso, hand, tracker_reported_velocity, velocity_unit, quality_flags (comma-joined), rejection_reason, decoder_version, calibration_profile_id, calibration_profile_version.
- [ ] CSV export includes a header block (comment lines) carrying session id, `calculation_version`, decoder version, per-hand calibration profile id + version, and the §8.5 velocity-representation label.
- [ ] JSON export bundles session metadata, timer_config, rounds, punch_events (with rejection_reason), session_metrics for every stored `calculation_version` / calibration combination, §9.5 quality metrics, connection interruptions, per-hand calibration profile id + version, decoder version, and the velocity-representation label.
- [ ] Both formats omit velocity fields when velocity is unavailable rather than emitting zeros.
- [ ] Filenames follow `punchcraft_<sessionId>_<isoWallTime>.{csv,json}`.
- [ ] Round-trip test parses the JSON export back into the domain types without loss.
- [ ] Terminology audit: no occurrences of force/power/energy in export column names or JSON keys (§4.3).

## Non-goals

- Cloud upload; sharing beyond the OS share sheet.

## Notes

- Files: `src/storage/exporters/SessionExporter.ts`, `src/app/(punchcraft)/history/[sessionId].tsx` share action.

epic.title: [EPIC] Phase 5 — Puncheokie program engine without Spotify
epic.body:
## Objectives

- Prove numbered sequences, stance mapping, and capability-aware scoring independently of any third-party music API (§22 Phase 5).
- Ship an end-to-end Puncheokie loop — author, run, score — using only visual and haptic cues so that Spotify integration in Phase 6 is additive rather than blocking.

## Milestones

- M24 — Program model & editor
- M25 — Stance mapping & cue runner
- M26 — Cue matching & capability-aware scoring

## Definition of done

The user can author and run a sequence workout, switch stance, and receive capability-appropriate completion results without Spotify (§22 Phase 5).

## Non-goals

- No Spotify authentication, playlist selection, or playback control (Phase 6).
- No app-generated audio prompts over third-party playback until policy review (§13.5).
- No claim of punch-technique accuracy when only hand data is available; label such results as hand-sequence match (§13.3).
- No overlap with Velocity Lab or punchCraft session engines beyond shared punch-event contracts.

## Sub-issues

GitHub auto-populates this list from the child issues linked to this epic.

issues.title: Define PunchProgram, ProgramRound, PunchCue domain types
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 5 / M24. Establish the Puncheokie program shape in the domain layer per §13.4 so downstream engine and UI code have a single source of truth. Lives under src/domain/programs/ per §16 and must not import RN/Expo/SQLite/BLE (§15.1).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `src/domain/programs/PunchProgram.ts` exports `PunchProgram`, `ProgramRound`, and `PunchCue` matching the interfaces in §13.4 verbatim (fields, optionality, and unions).
- [ ] `stance` on cues is the union `'inherit' | 'regular' | 'switch'`; program `defaultStance` is `'regular' | 'switch'`.
- [ ] `sequence: number[]` values are validated to be in 1..6 by a `validateProgram(p)` helper that returns typed errors, not throws.
- [ ] `targetVelocityZone` is the numeric literal union `1 | 2 | 3 | 4`.
- [ ] Module has zero runtime imports from `react-native`, `expo-*`, `expo-sqlite`, or `react-native-ble-plx`.

## Non-goals

- No persistence, no editor UI, no cue matching logic.

## Notes

See §13.4 example program fragment for Three-Round Fundamentals. Related files: src/domain/programs/ProgramEngine.ts (later), src/storage/repositories/ProgramRepository.ts (M24-03).

issues.title: Add SQLite migration for punch_programs, program_rounds, punch_cues, cue_results
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 5 / M24. Persistence for Puncheokie authoring and scoring per §17.1. Migration lives under src/storage/migrations/ per §16. Also stores the decoder/capability snapshot per cue result so future decoder improvements can recalculate scores (§13.6).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] New migration file creates `punch_programs` (id, name, description, version, default_stance, created_at, updated_at).
- [ ] Creates `program_rounds` (id, program_id FK, order_index, work_duration_ms, rest_after_ms).
- [ ] Creates `punch_cues` (id, round_id FK, start_offset_ms, duration_ms, stance, sequence_json, repeat, target_velocity_zone nullable, grace_before_ms, grace_after_ms, instruction nullable).
- [ ] Creates `cue_results` with columns listed in §17.1 (session_id, cue_id, expected_count, observed_count, correct_hand_count, correct_type_count, extra_count, average_velocity, completion_score) plus `decoder_version TEXT NOT NULL` and `capability_tier TEXT NOT NULL` for recalculation per §13.6.
- [ ] All FKs `ON DELETE CASCADE` from program → rounds → cues; `cue_results` references `sessions.id` and `punch_cues.id`.
- [ ] Indexes on `program_rounds.program_id`, `punch_cues.round_id`, `cue_results.session_id`.
- [ ] Migration runs forward cleanly on a fresh install and on a DB already migrated through Phase 4.

## Non-goals

- No seed data (see M24-04). No repository code (see M24-03).

## Notes

Sequence is stored as JSON text of `number[]`. Keep column names snake_case per existing tables.

issues.title: Implement ProgramRepository CRUD
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 5 / M24. Bridges domain PunchProgram objects (§13.4) to the SQLite tables added in M24-02. Per §16 lives at src/storage/repositories/ProgramRepository.ts. Domain layer stays unaware of SQLite (§15.1); repository handles JSON encoding of `sequence` and stance strings.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `listPrograms()`, `getProgram(id)`, `upsertProgram(p)`, `deleteProgram(id)` are exported and typed against domain types from M24-01.
- [ ] `getProgram` returns a fully hydrated program with rounds ordered by `order_index` and cues ordered by `start_offset_ms`.
- [ ] `upsertProgram` writes program + rounds + cues in a single transaction; deleting removed rounds/cues cascades.
- [ ] `version` and `updatedAt` are bumped by the repository on every upsert.
- [ ] Unit tests using an in-memory SQLite adapter cover round-trip encode/decode, add/remove of a cue, and cascade delete.

## Non-goals

- No editor UI. No cue-result reads/writes (owned by matcher in M26).

## Notes

Mirror the shape used by SessionRepository / DeviceRepository from earlier phases.

issues.title: Seed Three-Round Fundamentals program
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 5 / M24. Ship a canonical starter program so first-run users have something to try. Uses the example in §13.4 as the source of truth for the first cues; extended to three rounds per the program name. Owned by storage per the phase rule that schema/seed lives in the storage area.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A seed function inserts a program named exactly `Three-Round Fundamentals` on first launch if no program with that name exists.
- [ ] `defaultStance` is `regular`; contains three rounds, each with `workDurationMs: 180000` and `restAfterMs: 60000`.
- [ ] Round 1 begins with the two cues shown verbatim in §13.4 (1-2 x3 for 8000 ms starting at 0; switch 1-2-3 x2 for 10000 ms starting at 8000).
- [ ] Seed is idempotent — re-running does not duplicate the program or its rows.
- [ ] Seed is exercised by an integration test that loads via `ProgramRepository.getProgram` and asserts the round/cue counts and the first two cues match §13.4.

## Non-goals

- No UI to reset or re-seed from settings.

## Notes

Cue content for rounds 2 and 3 can be simple variations (e.g. 1-2-3-2, 1-2-5-2) at the implementer's discretion; document choices in a header comment.

issues.title: Build basic program editor
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 5 / M24. Minimal editor so a user can create/edit a Puncheokie program end-to-end per §13.4 and §22 Phase 5 task 2. Screen lives under src/app/ (Expo Router) and composes domain types from M24-01 through ProgramRepository (M24-03). On the phase DoD critical path (user must be able to author a sequence workout).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Program list screen shows all programs from `listPrograms()` with name and round count and links to the editor.
- [ ] Editor lets the user set program name, description, default stance (regular/switch), and add/remove/reorder rounds.
- [ ] Round editor lets the user set work and rest durations (ms) and add/remove/reorder cues.
- [ ] Cue editor lets the user set `sequence` (numbers 1-6 picker), `repeat`, `stance` (inherit/regular/switch), `startOffsetMs`, `durationMs`, and optional `targetVelocityZone`, `graceBeforeMs`, `graceAfterMs`, `instruction`.
- [ ] Save calls `upsertProgram`; validation errors from `validateProgram` are shown inline and prevent save.
- [ ] Duplicating and deleting a program work from the list screen.

## Non-goals

- No drag-to-reorder gestures required (up/down buttons acceptable). No sharing/import/export.

## Notes

Keep the editor stance-agnostic — numbering is lead/rear (§13.2); the runner will resolve to left/right at run time.

issues.title: Implement StanceMapper for lead/rear to left/right resolution
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 5 / M25. Central mapper from the internal lead/rear numbering (§13.2) to physical hand, honoring user regular stance (orthodox/southpaw) and per-cue stance overrides. Lives at src/domain/programs/StanceMapper.ts (§16), pure domain.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Exports `resolveHand(number: 1..6, effectiveStance: 'regular'|'switch', regularStance: 'orthodox'|'southpaw'): 'left'|'right'`.
- [ ] Exports `resolveEffectiveStance(cueStance, programDefaultStance)` implementing the `'inherit'` rule.
- [ ] For regular stance = orthodox, numbers 1/3/5 resolve to `left`, 2/4/6 to `right`; switch inverts.
- [ ] For regular stance = southpaw, numbers 1/3/5 resolve to `right`, 2/4/6 to `left`; switch inverts.
- [ ] Given a `sequence: number[]` and stance context, `resolveSequence` returns the corresponding `('left'|'right')[]` in order.
- [ ] Module has no imports from RN/Expo/SQLite/BLE (§15.1).

## Non-goals

- No UI. No matching or scoring — those live in M26.

## Notes

See §13.2 mapping table. The user-visible label switch always inverts, regardless of orthodox/southpaw.

issues.title: StanceMapper unit tests: orthodox and southpaw x switch
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 5 / M25. Explicit coverage for the §13.2 mapping matrix so regressions never silently invert a user's hand assignment. Test file lives under the domain package alongside StanceMapper.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Table-driven tests assert the resolved hand for every number 1..6 across all four combinations: (regular=orthodox, effective=regular), (regular=orthodox, effective=switch), (regular=southpaw, effective=regular), (regular=southpaw, effective=switch).
- [ ] Test verifies that switch inverts every mapping compared to the same regular-stance baseline.
- [ ] Test for `resolveEffectiveStance` covers cue `'inherit'` → program default (both regular and switch defaults) and cue `'regular'`/`'switch'` overriding the default.
- [ ] `resolveSequence([1,2,3], ...)` returns the expected hand array for each of the four combinations, including a southpaw-switch case.
- [ ] Tests run in CI with the domain test suite and require no hardware.

## Non-goals

- No integration tests with the cue runner (covered in M25-03/M26-01).

## Notes

See §13.3: with only hand data, this mapping is the ground truth for the hand-sequence match label.

issues.title: Implement ProgramEngine cue timer and round state machine
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 5 / M25. Drives a program through countdown → work → rest → next round → complete, emitting cue-active windows for the matcher. Lives at src/domain/programs/ProgramEngine.ts (§16). Uses the monotonic time source per §18.3 and stays pure domain (§15.1); UI subscribes via a store in src/state/useProgramStore.ts.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Engine states include `idle`, `countdown`, `work`, `rest`, `completed`; transitions are unit-tested with a fake clock.
- [ ] During `work`, the engine computes the current cue and next cue from `startOffsetMs` and `durationMs` and exposes them plus time remaining.
- [ ] Engine emits `cueWindowOpened` and `cueWindowClosed` events using `windowStart = cueStart - graceBefore` and `windowEnd = cueEnd + graceAfter` per §13.6.
- [ ] All cue/round timing derives from the monotonic clock source per §18.3 (no `Date.now()` for elapsed math); the clock is injected so tests can substitute a fake.
- [ ] Pause and resume preserve elapsed time correctly; abort transitions to `idle` without persisting partial results.
- [ ] Engine has no imports from RN/Expo/SQLite/BLE.
- [ ] Unit tests cover: two cues back-to-back, cue with grace overlapping neighbor, pause during rest, abort mid-work.

## Non-goals

- No event-to-cue matching (M26-01). No UI. No persistence of cue results (M26-03).

## Notes

Related: SessionEngine (Phase 4) for the state-machine pattern to mirror.

issues.title: Build live Puncheokie cue screen with visual and haptic cues
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 5 / M25. Realizes §13.5 cue presentation on top of the ProgramEngine (M25-03) and StanceMapper (M25-01). Route lives under src/app/, composes components from src/components/ (RoundTimer, PunchSequenceCard). On the phase DoD critical path (user must be able to run the sequence workout).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Screen shows: current stance, current numbered sequence in large type, lead/rear or left/right hand hints, repeat count, time remaining in the cue, next cue preview, round timer, actual punch count for the cue, sequence-match status, and (when supported) velocity-zone status per §13.5.
- [ ] A haptic pulse fires at cue start; sequence chevrons advance visually per matched punch (data source stubbed until M26-01 lands).
- [ ] No app-generated audio is played; a comment references §13.5 policy-review gate for future audio work.
- [ ] Pause/resume/abort controls call into the ProgramEngine; UI reflects state transitions.
- [ ] Screen renders correctly at tablet size in landscape (per punchCraft conventions).

## Non-goals

- No Spotify integration (Phase 6). No scoring UI (M26-03).
- No app-generated audio cues, tones, count-ins, or TTS pending Spotify policy review (§13.5).

## Notes

Use expo-haptics; guard for devices without haptics.

issues.title: Implement CueMatcher event-to-cue matching with acceptance windows
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 5 / M26. Assigns normalized punch events (§12.5) to expected cue slots per §13.6. Lives at src/domain/programs/CueMatcher.ts (§16). Consumes StanceMapper (M25-01) for expected hands and ProgramEngine windows (M25-03). Pure algorithm — no UI surface.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `matchEvent(event, openCues)` returns at most one assignment; one incoming event maps to at most one expected slot (§13.6 invariant) and matched events are removed from further consideration.
- [ ] Events are processed in event-time order; the matcher does not reorder based on wall clock.
- [ ] Acceptance window per cue is `[cueStart - graceBefore, cueEnd + graceAfter]` as in §13.6.
- [ ] Extra punches (no open cue, or cue already fully satisfied) are surfaced in the result with an `extra` outcome and remain visible — never dropped or merged away (§13.6 invariant).
- [ ] Hand mismatch and type mismatch are reported as distinct outcomes; type mismatch is only emitted when the decoder actually reported a type (§13.3).
- [ ] Recovered events with reliable tracker timestamps can be applied after reconnection into still-open (or gracefully-closed) windows.
- [ ] Unit tests cover: perfect run, hand mismatch, extras, overlapping graces (one event fits both — assigned to the earlier cue only, enforcing the one-slot invariant), late-arriving recovered event.

## Non-goals

- No scoring aggregation (M26-02). No persistence (M26-03).

## Notes

Matcher is pure and deterministic so cue results are recalculable when decoder capabilities improve (§13.6).

issues.title: Implement capability-aware scoring with hand-sequence match label
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 5 / M26. Aggregates CueMatcher outputs (M26-01) into per-cue and per-session scores per §13.3 and §13.6. Domain-only; consumes tracker capability flags from the protocol adapter (§12.3). Also evaluates the optional velocity-zone target (`cue.targetVelocityZone`) when the profile supports calibrated velocity.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Produces per-cue metrics: completion percentage, correct-hand percentage, timing-window percentage, technique-category percentage (only when type data is present), average velocity, target-zone percentage, extra-punch count (§13.6).
- [ ] When only hand data is available, the top-line score object exposes a label of exactly `hand-sequence match`; the code must not label the result as punch-technique accuracy (§13.3).
- [ ] When broad or distinct type data is available, the label upgrades to `technique-family match` or `technique match` respectively; capability tier is recorded on each cue result for later recalculation.
- [ ] Optional velocity-zone target: when `cue.targetVelocityZone` is set AND the active tracker profile exposes calibrated velocity, scoring emits a target-zone percentage (fraction of matched events whose tracker-reported velocity falls in the target zone 1..4) and labels it as an optional intensity-zone target per §13.3.
- [ ] When `cue.targetVelocityZone` is set but the profile does not expose calibrated velocity, the field is omitted from the result and a `capabilityGap` note is attached to the cue result — never a defaulted or zero value.
- [ ] Velocity zones (1..4) are only reported when the profile in use exposes calibrated velocity; otherwise the field is omitted rather than defaulted.
- [ ] Uses the terminology rule (§4.3) — no impact speed, force, power, energy, or punch strength; only tracker-reported velocity.
- [ ] Unit tests cover each of the capability tiers in §13.3 and assert the emitted label, plus the two velocity-zone branches (supported and unsupported).

## Non-goals

- No storage (M26-03). No matching (M26-01).

## Notes

Relates to §11.4 component boundaries: scoring stays in domain, not in UI or storage layers.

issues.title: Persist cue_results and render program summary screen
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 5 / M26. Closes the Puncheokie loop by writing the scoring output to `cue_results` (§17.1) and presenting a completion summary that satisfies the phase Definition of done (capability-appropriate completion results). Repository under src/storage/repositories/, summary screen under src/app/. On the phase DoD critical path.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] On program completion the app writes one row to `cue_results` per cue with the exact columns listed in §17.1: `session_id`, `cue_id`, `expected_count`, `observed_count`, `correct_hand_count`, `correct_type_count`, `extra_count`, `average_velocity`, `completion_score`.
- [ ] Each `cue_results` row also records `decoder_version` and `capability_tier` (from the protocol adapter and M26-02 capability tier) so results can be recalculated later when decoders improve (§13.6).
- [ ] Writes occur inside a single transaction alongside the parent `sessions` row (mode = `puncheokie`).
- [ ] Summary screen shows total completion percentage, per-round breakdown, hand-match percentage, and — only when supported — technique-family/technique percentage and velocity-zone percentage per §13.6.
- [ ] Summary displays the capability-tier label from M26-02 verbatim (e.g. `hand-sequence match`); does not claim technique accuracy when only hand data is available (§13.3).
- [ ] Extra punches are visible in a dedicated section with count and timestamps (§13.6).
- [ ] Summary uses the §4.3 terminology (tracker-reported velocity only).

## Non-goals

- No Spotify metadata on the summary (Phase 6). No sharing/export.

## Notes

Store `session_id` on the summary route so history (Phase 4) can link forward.

issues.title: CueMatcher fixture tests for hand-only, hand+type, and recovered-event cases
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 5 / M26. Locks matcher and scoring behavior against representative event streams so future decoder improvements do not silently change results. Fixtures live alongside CueMatcher tests; scoring assertions cover the §13.3 capability tiers and the §13.6 invariants (extras remain visible; one event → at most one slot).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Fixture 1 (hand only): sequence 1-2-3 in orthodox regular stance; asserts left-right-left match, label exactly `hand-sequence match`, no technique-family score emitted.
- [ ] Fixture 2 (hand + broad type): same sequence; asserts technique-family percentage present and label upgraded per M26-02.
- [ ] Fixture 3 (extras remain visible): the athlete throws an extra punch mid-cue; asserts the extra is present in the matcher output with an `extra` outcome, is not dropped, and completion percentage is unaffected (§13.6 invariant).
- [ ] Fixture 4 (recovered): an event with a reliable tracker timestamp arrives after the cue closed but within grace; asserts it is applied.
- [ ] Fixture 5 (southpaw switch): sequence 1-2 while southpaw regular + cue stance `switch`; asserts expected hands via StanceMapper are left-right.
- [ ] Fixture 6 (one-slot invariant): a single event whose timestamp falls inside two overlapping grace windows is assigned to exactly one cue (the earlier one) per §13.6; the other cue records no match for that event.
- [ ] Tests run headless in CI and require no hardware.

## Non-goals

- No end-to-end BLE integration test.

## Notes

Use normalized PunchEvent fixtures from src/protocol/fightcamp-v1/fixtures/ where available.

epic.title: [EPIC] Phase 6 — Spotify playlist connection
epic.body:
## Objectives

- Authorize one personal Spotify account via OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code with PKCE.
- Retrieve and select playlists the user is permitted to access under Development Mode.
- Open selected content in the installed Spotify Android app via deep link.
- Keep workout timing fully independent of Spotify playback state.

## Milestones

- M27 — Spotify PKCE authorization & secure tokens
- M28 — Playlist selection, caching & deep link

## Definition of done

An allowlisted user can connect Spotify, choose an accessible playlist, open it in the Spotify app, return to Puncheokie, and run a program without Spotify controlling the workout clock. Tokens live only in `expo-secure-store` (§20.3); no client secret exists anywhere in the repo (§14.2); Puncheokie runs correctly with Spotify disconnected or failing (§14.3, §14.6); UI tolerates followed non-owned playlists whose metadata is visible but whose items are unavailable (§14.3); 401/403/429 handling matches §14.8; tokens are redacted from logs and diagnostic exports (§20.3, §20.4); the Spotify policy gate (§14.6) has been reviewed and documented prior to any public distribution.

## Non-goals

- Embedded audio streaming, Web Playback SDK, or App Remote SDK integration.
- Beat detection, audio-feature analysis, or song-synchronized cue choreography.
- Playback-control scopes (`user-modify-playback-state`, etc.) or Premium-gated player endpoints.
- Downloading, caching, or transforming Spotify audio content or artwork.
- Any workflow that couples the Puncheokie timer to Spotify player state.

## Sub-issues
